Tags are case-insensitive for comparison purposes (e.g., "Politics" and "politics" are treated as the same tag). Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed during normalization. Duplicate tags are automatically removed.

models.description:
Junction table implementing the many-to-many relationship between articles and tags.

This table enables flexible article categorization beyond section-based organization. Users can associate up to 15 tags per article during creation or editing. The table supports tag-based article discovery and filtering workflows.

**Cascade Behavior**: When an article is deleted, all its tag associations are automatically removed. Tags themselves persist independently and can be reused across other articles, supporting tag normalization and platform-wide consistency.

**Business Rules**:
- Maximum 15 tags per article (enforced at application layer)
- Tag values are case-insensitive and normalized to lowercase in {@link discussion_board_tags.value}
- Duplicate tag associations for the same article are prevented by unique constraint

models.description:
User submissions to become administrators with reason, status (pending/approved/rejected), and review workflow tracking.

This table implements the administrator request system where authenticated users submit requests to become administrators. Super administrators review pending requests and approve or reject them with optional notes. The system enforces the rule that a user may have only one pending request at any time through a unique constraint on (requester_id, status) for pending status.

All request records are retained for audit purposes regardless of outcome. Request history is preserved to support merit-based evaluation and transparency in the governance process. When a request is approved, the requester's permission level is updated to ADMINISTRATOR in the {@link discussion_board_users} table.

Key relationships:
- {@link discussion_board_users} (requester): The user who submitted the admin request
- {@link discussion_board_users} (reviewer): The super administrator who reviewed the request

Immutable audit trail records of administrator hierarchy changes within the platform.

Captures promotion and demotion actions between regular administrator and super administrator roles. Each record tracks the acting administrator (who performed the action), the target administrator (who was affected), the action type, and an optional reason.

This table supports the governance requirements where:
- Super administrators can promote regular administrators to super administrator status
- Super administrators can demote other super administrators to regular administrator status
- Self-demotion prevention is enforced at the application layer

Records are append-only for compliance and audit purposes. Historical data is never modified or deleted.

This table maintains a complete audit trail of unbanning decisions for compliance and administrative review. models.description:
Immutable audit trail for all ban and unban administrative actions.

This table serves as a compliance-focused, append-only record of all user ban and unban operations performed by administrators. Each entry captures the complete context of the action including the affected user, the administrator who performed the action, the reason provided, and timestamp.

**Key Characteristics:**
- Immutable: Records cannot be modified or deleted once created
- Persistent: Records survive even when referenced users or ban records are deleted
- Compliance-ready: Supports filtering by date range, administrator, and action type

**Action Types:**
- BAN: Records when a user is banned from the platform
- UNBAN: Records when a previously banned user has their access restored

**Relationships:**
- References {@link discussion_board_users} for both target user and administrator
- May reference {@link discussion_board_bans} for unban actions to link back to the original ban record

**Query Patterns:**
- Filter by action type for reporting
- Filter by administrator for accountability tracking
- Filter by date range for compliance audits
- Filter by target user for user history viewing

foreignFields.description: The user who was banned or unbanned. Nullable to support FR-AUDIT-005: when a user account is deleted, audit records are retained with anonymized references. {@link discussion_board_users.id}
foreignFields.name: discussion_board_user_id

foreignFields.description: The administrator who performed the ban or unban action. Nullable to support FR-AUDIT-005: when an administrator account is deleted, audit records are retained with anonymized references. {@link discussion_board_users.id}
foreignFields.name: actor_id

foreignFields.description: Reference to the original ban record for unban actions. NULL for BAN actions. Used to trace the complete ban lifecycle. Nullable to preserve audit records if the original ban record is deleted. {@link discussion_board_bans.id}
foreignFields.name: discussion_board_ban_id

### `discussion_board_users`

User accounts with email/password authentication, permission levels
(MEMBER, ADMINISTRATOR, SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR), ban status, and profile
information (display name, bio).

Each user has a unique email address for authentication, a password hash
for security, and a permission level that determines their access rights
within the platform. The permission_level field stores one of three
values: MEMBER (regular user), ADMINISTRATOR (can moderate content,
manage sections, ban users), or SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR (can also manage
admin hierarchy and approve admin requests).

The profile fields (display_name and bio) provide identity information
visible to other users. The is_banned flag indicates whether the user is
currently prohibited from logging in, though their existing content
remains visible.

Users reference a citizen sequence ID for human-readable sequential
identification. Related entities include sessions ({@link
discussion_board_user_sessions}), password resets ({@link
discussion_board_user_password_resets}), admin requests ({@link
discussion_board_user_admin_requests}), and audit logs ({@link
discussion_board_user_audit_logs}).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `citizen_id`
  > Sequential ID reference from the citizen sequence for human-readable user
  > identification. [discussion_board_user_citizens.id](#discussion_board_user_citizens)
- `banned_by`
  > Administrator who banned this user, if applicable. Null when user is not
  > banned or was banned by a super admin who was later demoted. {@link
  > discussion_board_users.id}
- `email`
  > Unique email address used for authentication. Must be a valid email
  > format and unique across all users.
- `password_hash`
  > Secure hash of the user's password. Never store plain text passwords.
  > Uses bcrypt or similar secure hashing algorithm.
- `display_name`
  > User's display name shown on their profile and alongside their content.
  > Visible to other users.
- `bio`
  > Optional biographical text for the user's profile. Can be null for users
  > who haven't filled it in.
- `permission_level`
  > User's permission level determining their access rights. One of: MEMBER,
  > ADMINISTRATOR, or SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR.
- `is_banned`
  > Flag indicating whether the user is currently banned from the platform.
  > Banned users cannot log in but their content remains visible.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the user account was created.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the user account was last updated (profile changes,
  > permission changes, etc.).
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when the user account was soft-deleted. Null for active
  > accounts. When a user deletes their account, their articles and comments
  > are cascade deleted.

### `discussion_board_user_sessions`

JWT authentication sessions for users, tracking access tokens, refresh
tokens, and connection metadata across multiple devices.

Each session represents a single authenticated device/browser instance.
The refresh token uniquely identifies the session and enables token
rotation. Access tokens are short-lived (15-30 minutes) while refresh
tokens have longer expiration periods (7-30 days).

Sessions support multi-device authentication, allowing users to be logged
in on multiple devices simultaneously. Connection metadata (IP, href,
referrer) provides security auditing and fraud detection capabilities.

Relationship: Each session belongs to exactly one {@link
discussion_board_users}. Sessions are cascade-deleted when the parent
user is deleted.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_user_id`
  > The user who owns this session. References {@link
  > discussion_board_users.id}. A user can have multiple active sessions
  > across different devices.
- `access_token`
  > JWT access token for API authentication. Short-lived token (typically
  > 15-30 minutes) used to authenticate API requests. Can be regenerated
  > using the refresh token.
- `refresh_token`
  > JWT refresh token for session persistence. Long-lived token (typically
  > 7-30 days) used to obtain new access tokens. This uniquely identifies the
  > session.
- `ip`
  > IP address from which the session was initiated. Used for security
  > auditing, geographic analysis, and fraud detection.
- `href`
  > URL of the page where the login was initiated. Captures the entry point
  > for the authentication request, useful for tracking user flows.
- `referrer`
  > Referrer URL that led the user to the login page. Useful for tracking
  > traffic sources and user navigation paths.
- `user_agent`
  > User agent string from the client browser. Identifies the browser,
  > operating system, and device type for session management.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the session was created (login time). Records the initial
  > authentication moment.
- `expired_at`
  > Timestamp when the refresh token expires. Marks the end of the session's
  > validity period. Sessions can be terminated earlier through logout or
  > revocation.

### `discussion_board_user_password_resets`

Password reset tokens for email-based password recovery. Stores secure
tokens with expiration timestamps that allow users to reset their
passwords. Each token is single-use and should be deleted after
successful password reset. Tokens expire after a defined period
(typically 15-60 minutes) for security. A user may have multiple reset
requests over time, but typically only one active token at a time.
References the [discussion_board_users](#discussion_board_users) table for user association.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_user_id`
  > The user who requested the password reset. References {@link
  > discussion_board_users.id}.
- `token`
  > Secure password reset token (hashed using cryptographic algorithm). This
  > token is sent to the user's email and must be presented to complete the
  > password reset. Should be generated using a cryptographically secure
  > random generator.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the password reset request was created. Used for audit
  > logging and determining token age.
- `expires_at`
  > Timestamp when the password reset token expires. After this time, the
  > token is invalid and a new reset request must be made. Non-null by
  > default for security - all tokens must have a defined expiration period
  > (typically 15-60 minutes).

### `discussion_board_user_admin_requests`

Administrator request records submitted by users seeking administrative
privileges. Each request captures the user's reason for requesting admin
status and tracks the approval workflow from submission through review by
super administrators.

Requests progress through three states: pending (awaiting review),
approved (user granted admin status), and rejected (request declined).
Super administrators review pending requests and record their decision
with optional notes. Users may submit new requests after rejection.

Business rules enforced:
- Only one pending request per user at any time
- Users with existing admin status cannot submit requests
- Banned users cannot submit requests
- Request reason must be substantive (minimum 50 characters)

Related entities: [discussion_board_users](#discussion_board_users) for requester identity,
[discussion_board_users](#discussion_board_users) for reviewer attribution.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_user_id`
  > The user who submitted this administrator request. References {@link
  > discussion_board_users.id}. A user may have multiple requests over time
  > (e.g., after rejection), but only one pending request at any given time.
- `reviewer_id`
  > The super administrator who reviewed and decided on this request.
  > References [discussion_board_users.id](#discussion_board_users). Null while request is in
  > pending status. Populated when request is approved or rejected.
- `reason`
  > The user's explanation of why they should become an administrator. Must
  > be substantive and detailed, with a minimum of 50 characters to ensure
  > meaningful reasoning is provided. Used by super administrators during
  > review to assess the request.
- `status`
  > Current state of the administrator request. Values: 'pending' (awaiting
  > review by super administrator), 'approved' (user granted administrator
  > privileges), 'rejected' (request declined). Only pending requests appear
  > in super administrators' review queue.
- `review_notes`
  > Optional notes provided by the reviewing super administrator when
  > approving or rejecting the request. May contain feedback, conditions, or
  > explanation of the decision. Null if no notes were provided or request is
  > still pending.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the administrator request was submitted by the user. Used
  > for chronological ordering of requests and calculating time elapsed in
  > pending status.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the request was last modified. Updated when status changes
  > from pending to approved or rejected, or when review notes are added.
- `reviewed_at`
  > Timestamp when the request was reviewed by a super administrator. Set
  > when status transitions from pending to approved or rejected. Null while
  > request is pending.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when the request was soft-deleted. Admin requests are typically
  > retained for audit purposes but may be soft-deleted for moderation or
  > cleanup purposes.

### `discussion_board_user_audit_logs`

Immutable audit trail of user-related administrative actions including
bans, unbans, permission level changes (promotions/demotions), and other
authorization events. Provides comprehensive logging for compliance and
security auditing.

Each audit entry captures the target user, the type of action performed,
the administrator who performed it (if applicable), the reason for the
action, and the timestamp. Used for security monitoring, compliance
reporting, and accountability tracking.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_user_id`
  > The user who was the target of this audit action. References {@link
  > discussion_board_users.id}.
- `actor_user_id`
  > The administrator who performed this action. Nullable for
  > system-initiated actions. References [discussion_board_users.id](#discussion_board_users).
- `action`
  > Type of audit action performed. Values: 'password_change' (user changed
  > their own password), 'account_deleted' (user deleted their account),
  > 'permission_granted' (user promoted to admin/super admin),
  > 'permission_revoked' (user demoted from admin), 'banned' (user was
  > banned), 'unbanned' (user was unbanned).
- `reason`
  > Human-readable reason or description for the action. Required for
  > administrative actions (bans, unbans, permission changes), optional for
  > user-initiated actions.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the audit action occurred.

### `discussion_board_sections`

Discussion board sections that organize articles by topic categories such
as Politics, Economy, and Current Affairs. Each section has a unique name
and description, managed exclusively by administrators. Sections serve as
the primary organizational structure for articles, and deletion of a
section triggers cascade deletion of all articles within that section.
The table tracks both the creator and last modifier administrator for
audit purposes.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `creator_id`
  > The administrator who created this section. References {@link
  > discussion_board_users.id}.
- `modifier_id`
  > The administrator who last modified this section. References {@link
  > discussion_board_users.id}.
- `name`
  > Unique name of the section. Used for display and identification. Must be
  > unique across all sections.
- `description`
  > Detailed description of the section's purpose and the types of
  > discussions it contains.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the section was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the section was last updated.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when the section was soft-deleted. Null if the section is
  > active. Soft delete preserves section data for audit trails while hiding
  > from active browsing.

### `discussion_board_articles`

Primary content entity for discussion board articles.

Articles are the main discussion content created by users within
sections. Each article has a title, content body, is assigned to exactly
one section, and has an author (user). Articles support soft deletion to
preserve banned users' content visibility.

Relationships:
- Belongs to a [discussion_board_section](#discussion_board_section) via section reference
- Authored by a [discussion_board_user](#discussion_board_user) via user reference
- Has associated [discussion_board_article_files](#discussion_board_article_files) for file attachments
- Has associated [discussion_board_article_images](#discussion_board_article_images) for image
attachments
- Has associated [discussion_board_article_tags](#discussion_board_article_tags) for tag associations
- Has associated [discussion_board_comments](#discussion_board_comments) for discussion

Business rules:
- Title: 3-200 characters, required
- Content: 10-50,000 characters, required
- Author can edit their own articles
- Author can delete their own articles (soft delete)
- Administrators can delete any article
- Cascade deletes attachments, images, tags, and comments when hard deleted

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_section_id`
  > Section where this article is published. Every article must belong to
  > exactly one section. References [discussion_board_sections.id](#discussion_board_sections).
- `discussion_board_user_id`
  > Author of this article. The user who created and owns this article.
  > References [discussion_board_users.id](#discussion_board_users).
- `title`
  > Article title. Must be between 3 and 200 characters. Used for display and
  > search indexing.
- `content`
  > Article content body. Text content between 10 and 50,000 characters.
  > Supports plain text formatting.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the article was created. Automatically set on article
  > creation.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the article was last updated. Updated automatically when
  > article is modified.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when the article was soft-deleted. Null if article is active.
  > Used to preserve banned users' content visibility while hiding from
  > normal browsing.

File attachments for articles storing PDF, document, spreadsheet,
presentation, and archive files.

Each file attachment records the original filename as uploaded by the
user, the server-side storage path, file size in bytes for quota
enforcement (10MB individual limit, 50MB total per article), and MIME
type for validation. Supports common document formats including PDF, Word
documents (DOC/DOCX), Excel spreadsheets (XLS/XLSX), PowerPoint
presentations (PPT/PPTX), and archive files (ZIP, RAR, 7Z).

Files are cascade deleted when their parent article is deleted. Maximum
10 files per article enforced at application layer.

- `storage_path`
  > Server-side storage path where the file is physically stored. Used for
  > file retrieval and deletion operations.
- `file_size`
  > File size in bytes. Used for enforcing the 10MB individual file limit and
  > 50MB total limit per article.
- `mime_type`
  > MIME type of the file (e.g., application/pdf,
  > application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document).
  > Used for content-type headers during download and file type validation.
- `created_at`

  > attachments.

Image attachments for discussion board articles. Stores JPEG, PNG, GIF,
WebP, and BMP images with original filename for display, storage path,
file size in bytes, MIME type, and pixel dimensions. Limited to 20 images
per article with 5MB individual file limit and 8000x8000 maximum
dimensions. Cascade deleted when parent article is removed. Managed
through article creation and editing operations.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_article_id`
  > Reference to the article this image belongs to. {@link
  > discussion_board_articles.id}
- `original_filename`
  > Original filename as uploaded by the user, preserved for display
  > purposes. Used when users download the image to provide the original
  > filename.
- `storage_path`
  > Unique storage path where the image file is physically stored.
  > System-generated path to prevent filename conflicts and security issues.
- `file_size`
  > Size of the image file in bytes. Maximum allowed is 5MB (5,242,880
  > bytes). Used for validation and storage quota tracking.
- `mime_type`
  > MIME type of the image. Supported values: image/jpeg, image/png,
  > image/gif, image/webp, image/bmp. Used for content-type headers when
  > serving images.
- `width`
  > Image width in pixels. Maximum allowed is 8000 pixels. Validated during
  > upload to ensure image integrity and dimension compliance.
- `height`
  > Image height in pixels. Maximum allowed is 8000 pixels. Validated during
  > upload to ensure image integrity and dimension compliance.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the image was uploaded and attached to the article.

### `discussion_board_tags`

Master table for unique tag values used in article categorization and
discovery.

Tags provide flexible, user-defined categorization beyond the
section-based structure. Each tag is a free-form text value normalized to
lowercase, supporting alphanumeric characters, hyphens, and underscores
only. Tags persist independently of articles and are reused across the
platform.

Tags are associated with articles through the {@link
discussion_board_article_tags} junction table, enabling many-to-many
relationships. Each article can have up to 15 tags. Tags support
case-insensitive comparison and automatic duplicate removal through the
normalization process.

The unique constraint on the value field ensures tag uniqueness across
the platform. Tags can be used for article filtering (single or multiple
tags with OR logic) and discovery through the tag-based browsing
interface.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `value`
  > Normalized tag value in lowercase. Must be 1-50 characters containing
  > only alphanumeric characters, hyphens (-), and underscores (_). Tags are
  > case-insensitive for comparison purposes (e.g., "Politics" and "politics"
  > are treated as the same tag). Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed
  > during normalization. Duplicate tags are automatically removed.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the tag was first created. Automatically set upon tag
  > creation.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the tag record was last updated. Initially matches
  > created_at on creation.

### `discussion_board_article_tags`

Junction table implementing the many-to-many relationship between
articles and tags.

This table enables flexible article categorization beyond section-based
organization. Users can associate up to 15 tags per article during
creation or editing. The table supports tag-based article discovery and
filtering workflows.

**Cascade Behavior**: When an article is deleted, all its tag
associations are automatically removed. Tags themselves persist
independently and can be reused across other articles, supporting tag
normalization and platform-wide consistency.

**Business Rules**:
- Maximum 15 tags per article (enforced at application layer)
- Tag values are case-insensitive and normalized to lowercase in {@link
discussion_board_tags.value}
- Duplicate tag associations for the same article are prevented by unique
constraint

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_article_id`
  > Reference to the tagged article. Uses cascade deletion to automatically
  > remove tag associations when the parent article is deleted, maintaining
  > referential integrity without orphaned records.
  >
  > Target article's [discussion_board_articles.id](#discussion_board_articles).
- `discussion_board_tag_id`
  > Reference to the associated tag. Preserves the tag record when
  > article-tag associations are deleted, allowing tag reuse across the
  > platform and maintaining the master tag registry.
  >
  > Target tag's [discussion_board_tags.id](#discussion_board_tags).
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the tag was associated with the article. Used for auditing
  > tag assignments and supporting chronological queries if needed.

## Comments

```mermaid
erDiagram
"discussion_board_comments" {
  String id PK
  String citizen_id FK,UK
  String discussion_board_article_id FK
  String discussion_board_user_id FK
  String content
  DateTime created_at
  DateTime updated_at "nullable"
  DateTime deleted_at "nullable"
}
```

### `discussion_board_comments`

Single-level comments attached to articles with author reference, content
(up to 10,000 characters), creation and edit timestamps, and soft delete
flag for audit preservation. Comments are sorted chronologically (oldest
first) to maintain natural conversation flow. Each comment belongs to
exactly one article and is written by one user. Administrators can delete
any comment for moderation purposes, while users can only delete their
own comments.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `citizen_id`
  > Sequential citizen identifier for human-readable comment numbering.
  > References [discussion_board_comment_citizens.id](#discussion_board_comment_citizens).
- `discussion_board_article_id`
  > Reference to the parent article. [discussion_board_articles.id](#discussion_board_articles).
  > Comments are cascade deleted when the article is deleted.
- `discussion_board_user_id`
  > Reference to the comment author. [discussion_board_users.id](#discussion_board_users).
  > Comments are cascade deleted when the user account is deleted.
- `content`
  > The comment body text. Must contain at least 1 non-whitespace character
  > and cannot exceed 10,000 characters. Leading and trailing whitespace is
  > trimmed before storage.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the comment was posted. Automatically set on creation and
  > never modified.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the comment was last edited. Null if the comment has never
  > been edited. Updated only when content is modified.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when the comment was soft-deleted. Null for active comments.
  > When set, the comment is excluded from public display but preserved for
  > audit purposes.

## Administration

```mermaid
erDiagram

  String id PK
  String requester_id FK
  String reviewer_id FK "nullable"
  String reason
  String status
  String review_notes "nullable"
  DateTime created_at
  DateTime updated_at
  DateTime reviewed_at "nullable"
}
"discussion_board_admin_hierarchy_actions" {
  String id PK
  String actor_id FK
  String target_id FK
  String action_type
  String reason "nullable"
  DateTime created_at
}
"discussion_board_admin_action_logs" {
  String id PK
  String administrator_id FK
  String original_author_id FK "nullable"
  String action_type
  String target_type
  String target_id
  String target_title
  String reason "nullable"
  String ip
  String user_agent "nullable"
  DateTime created_at
}
```

### `discussion_board_admin_requests`

User submissions to become administrators with reason, status
(pending/approved/rejected), and review workflow tracking.

This table implements the administrator request system where
authenticated users submit requests to become administrators. Super
administrators review pending requests and approve or reject them with
optional notes. The system enforces the rule that a user may have only
one pending request at any time through a unique constraint on
(requester_id, status) for pending status.

All request records are retained for audit purposes regardless of
outcome. Request history is preserved to support merit-based evaluation
and transparency in the governance process. When a request is approved,
the requester's permission level is updated to ADMINISTRATOR in the
[discussion_board_users](#discussion_board_users) table.

Key relationships:
- [discussion_board_users](#discussion_board_users) (requester): The user who submitted the
admin request
- [discussion_board_users](#discussion_board_users) (reviewer): The super administrator who
reviewed the request

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `requester_id`
  > The user who submitted this administrator request. References {@link
  > discussion_board_users.id}.
- `reviewer_id`
  > The super administrator who reviewed this request. Null if the request is
  > still pending. References [discussion_board_users.id](#discussion_board_users).
- `reason`
  > User's explanation of why they should become an administrator. Must be at
  > least 50 characters to ensure meaningful justification.
- `status`
  > Current state of the administrator request. Valid values: 'pending'
  > (awaiting review), 'approved' (user granted admin status), 'rejected'
  > (request denied). Users may submit new requests after rejection.
- `review_notes`
  > Optional notes from the super administrator who reviewed this request.
  > May contain explanation for approval or rejection decision. Null if
  > request is pending.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the administrator request was submitted.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the administrator request was last modified.
- `reviewed_at`
  > Timestamp when the request was reviewed by a super administrator. Null if
  > the request is still pending.

### `discussion_board_admin_hierarchy_actions`

Immutable audit trail records of administrator hierarchy changes within
the platform.

Captures promotion and demotion actions between regular administrator and
super administrator roles. Each record tracks the acting administrator
(who performed the action), the target administrator (who was affected),
the action type, and an optional reason.

This table supports the governance requirements where:
- Super administrators can promote regular administrators to super
administrator status
- Super administrators can demote other super administrators to regular
administrator status
- Self-demotion prevention is enforced at the application layer

Records are append-only for compliance and audit purposes. Historical
data is never modified or deleted.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `actor_id`
  > The administrator who performed the hierarchy action (promoter or
  > demoter). References [discussion_board_users.id](#discussion_board_users).
- `target_id`
  > The administrator who was affected by the hierarchy action (promoted or
  > demoted). References [discussion_board_users.id](#discussion_board_users).
- `action_type`
  > The type of hierarchy action performed. Valid values are 'PROMOTION'
  > (regular admin to super admin) or 'DEMOTION' (super admin to regular
  > admin).
- `reason`
  > Optional explanation for the hierarchy action. May contain justification
  > for the promotion or demotion decision.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the hierarchy action was performed. Records are immutable
  > after creation.

### `discussion_board_admin_action_logs`

Comprehensive audit trail of all administrative actions including content
moderation (article/comment deletion), section management
(create/edit/delete), user banning/unbanning, admin hierarchy changes,
and admin request reviews. This table serves as the single source of
truth for all administrative accountability, supporting filtering by date
range, administrator, and action type for compliance and audit purposes.
Logs are immutable and cannot be modified or deleted, including by super
administrators.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `administrator_id`
  > The administrator who performed this action. References {@link
  > discussion_board_users.id}.
- `original_author_id`
  > Reference to the user who created the original content that was acted
  > upon. Applicable for ARTICLE_DELETE and COMMENT_DELETE actions. Null for
  > actions that don't involve user-created content (SECTION_*, BAN_USER,
  > UNBAN_USER, PROMOTE_ADMIN, DEMOTE_ADMIN, APPROVE_REQUEST,
  > REJECT_REQUEST). References [discussion_board_users.id](#discussion_board_users).
- `action_type`
  > The type of administrative action performed. Values: ARTICLE_DELETE
  > (moderation), COMMENT_DELETE (moderation), SECTION_CREATE, SECTION_EDIT,
  > SECTION_DELETE (section management), BAN_USER, UNBAN_USER (user
  > management), PROMOTE_ADMIN, DEMOTE_ADMIN (hierarchy management),
  > APPROVE_REQUEST, REJECT_REQUEST (admin request workflow).
- `target_type`
  > The type of entity that was acted upon. Values: ARTICLE, COMMENT,
  > SECTION, USER, ADMIN_REQUEST. Used with target_id to identify the
  > affected entity.
- `target_id`
  > UUID of the entity that was acted upon. References the primary key of the
  > target table determined by target_type (discussion_board_articles,
  > discussion_board_comments, discussion_board_sections,
  > discussion_board_users, or discussion_board_admin_requests). Polymorphic
  > reference validated at application level.
- `target_title`
  > Human-readable title or truncated preview of the affected content. For
  > articles: article title. For comments: first 100 characters. For
  > sections: section name. For users: display name. For admin requests:
  > requester display name.
- `reason`
  > Optional reason or notes provided by the administrator for this action.
  > Required for ban actions (10-1000 characters), optional for other action
  > types. Used for ban reasons, deletion justifications, and review notes.
- `ip`
  > IP address of the administrator at the time of action. Captured for
  > security audit and accountability purposes.
- `user_agent`
  > User agent string of the administrator's browser/client at the time of
  > action. Captured for device identification and security auditing.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the administrative action was performed. Automatically set
  > upon creation.

### `discussion_board_bans`

Records of user bans performed by administrators.

Each ban record captures the target user, the administrator who performed
the ban,
the reason for the ban (10-1000 characters), and the timestamp. Ban
records are
immutable and persist for audit purposes even after unbanning.

Related tables:
- [discussion_board_users](#discussion_board_users) - Target users and administrator actors
- [discussion_board_unbans](#discussion_board_unbans) - Records of ban removal
- [discussion_board_ban_histories](#discussion_board_ban_histories) - Immutable audit trail

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_user_id`: The banned user who cannot login. [discussion_board_users.id](#discussion_board_users).
- `discussion_board_administrator_id`
  > The administrator who performed the ban action. {@link
  > discussion_board_users.id}.
- `reason`
  > Reason for the ban, recorded for transparency and audit. Must be between
  > 10 and 1000 characters.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the ban was created.

### `discussion_board_unbans`

Records unban actions that reverse active ban records. Each unban
references the original ban record, the administrator who performed the
unban, and includes a required reason text (10-1000 characters). This
table maintains a complete audit trail of unbanning decisions for
compliance and administrative review. One-to-one relationship with {@link
discussion_board_bans} ensures each ban can only be reversed once.
Supports the administrative workflow for restoring user access after ban
appeals or policy reversals.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_ban_id`
  > Reference to the original ban record being reversed. Each ban can only
  > have one unban action, creating a one-to-one relationship. {@link
  > discussion_board_bans.id}
- `administrator_id`
  > The administrator who performed the unban action. References the users
  > table since administrators are users with elevated permissions. {@link
  > discussion_board_users.id}
- `reason`
  > The reason for unbanning the user. Required text field with minimum 10
  > characters and maximum 1,000 characters. Provides documentation for the
  > administrative decision and supports audit requirements. Stored as
  > plaintext without markdown or HTML interpretation.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the unban action was performed. Records when the user's
  > access was restored.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the unban record was last modified. Typically unchanged
  > after initial creation as unban records are generally immutable.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp for soft deletion of the unban record. Used for audit
  > preservation when records are administratively removed.

### `discussion_board_ban_histories`

Immutable audit trail for all ban and unban administrative actions.

This table serves as a compliance-focused, append-only record of all user
ban and unban operations performed by administrators. Each entry captures
the complete context of the action including the affected user, the
administrator who performed the action, the reason provided, and
timestamp.

**Key Characteristics:**
- Immutable: Records cannot be modified or deleted once created
- Persistent: Records survive even when referenced users or ban records
are deleted
- Compliance-ready: Supports filtering by date range, administrator, and
action type

**Action Types:**
- BAN: Records when a user is banned from the platform
- UNBAN: Records when a previously banned user has their access restored

**Relationships:**
- References [discussion_board_users](#discussion_board_users) for both target user and
administrator
- May reference [discussion_board_bans](#discussion_board_bans) for unban actions to link
back to the original ban record

**Query Patterns:**
- Filter by action type for reporting
- Filter by administrator for accountability tracking
- Filter by date range for compliance audits
- Filter by target user for user history viewing

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_user_id`
  > The user who was banned or unbanned. Nullable to support FR-AUDIT-005:
  > when a user account is deleted, audit records are retained with
  > anonymized references. [discussion_board_users.id](#discussion_board_users)
- `actor_id`
  > The administrator who performed the ban or unban action. Nullable to
  > support FR-AUDIT-005: when an administrator account is deleted, audit
  > records are retained with anonymized references. {@link
  > discussion_board_users.id}
- `discussion_board_ban_id`
  > Reference to the original ban record for unban actions. NULL for BAN
  > actions. Used to trace the complete ban lifecycle. Nullable to preserve
  > audit records if the original ban record is deleted. {@link
  > discussion_board_bans.id}
- `action_type`
  > Type of administrative action performed. BAN indicates a user was banned
  > from the platform; UNBAN indicates a previously banned user had their
  > access restored. Used for filtering and reporting.
- `reason`
  > The reason text provided for the ban or unban action. Required for all
  > actions (minimum 10 characters, maximum 1,000 characters as per business
  > rules). Stored in plaintext without markdown or HTML interpretation.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the ban or unban action was executed. Used for
  > chronological sorting and date range filtering in audit reports.
  > Automatically recorded by the system at the time of action.

instruction:
## User Account APIs
- Users sign up with email and password
- Users log in with email and password
- Users can change their password
- Users can delete their account (all their articles and comments are also deleted)

## User Profile APIs
- Each user has a profile with: display name and bio text
- Users can edit their display name and bio
- Users can view other users' profiles
- A user's profile shows:
  - Their display name and bio
  - A list of all articles they have written
  - A list of all comments they have written

## Section APIs
- The board is divided into sections (e.g., Politics, Economy, Current Affairs)
- Sections are created and managed by administrators only
- Each section has: name and description
- Users can view the list of all sections
- Users can browse articles within a specific section

## Article APIs
- Users can create articles in any section
- Every article has:
  - Title (required)
  - Content (required, text)
  - Section (required, must choose one section)
- Users can attach files to their articles
- Users can attach images to their articles
- Multiple files and images can be attached to a single article
- Users can add tags to their articles (free text, multiple tags allowed)
- Users can edit their own articles (title, content, attachments, tags)
- Users can delete their own articles

## Article List APIs
- Users can view the list of articles in a section
- The list is paginated
- Each article in the list shows: title, author, tags, comment count, and time posted
- The list does not show the full content (only title)
- Users can sort articles by:
  - Newest first
  - Oldest first

## Article Detail APIs
- Users can view a single article with its full content
- The article page shows: title, author, content, attachments, tags, and time posted
- Users can download attached files and images

## Article Search APIs
- Users can search articles by title or content
- Search results are paginated
- Users can filter articles by tags

## Comment APIs
- Users can write comments on articles
- Comments are single-level only (no nested replies)
- Users can view all comments on an article
- Comments are sorted by oldest first
- Each comment shows: author, content, and time posted
- Users can edit their own comments
- Users can delete their own comments

## Administrator Request APIs
- Any user can submit a request to become an administrator
- The request includes a reason (text)
- Super administrators can view the list of pending requests
- Super administrators can approve or reject requests
- When approved, the user becomes a regular administrator

## Administrator Management APIs
- There are two grades: regular administrator and super administrator
- Super administrators can promote regular administrators to super administrator
- Super administrators can demote other super administrators to regular administrator
- Super administrators cannot demote themselves

## Administrator Capabilities APIs
- Administrators can do everything regular users can do (write articles, comments, etc.)
- Administrators can create, edit, and delete sections
- Administrators can delete any article
- Administrators can delete any comment
- Administrators can ban users
- Administrators can unban users
- Administrators can view the list of banned users

## Banning APIs
- Banned users cannot log in to the platform
- Banned users' existing articles and comments remain visible
- When a user is banned, a reason is recorded
- Administrators can view the ban reason for each banned user

operations.specification: Implementation: 1) Validate email format and check uniqueness against discussion_board_users.email (unique constraint). 2) Validate password meets security requirements: minimum 8 characters, at least one uppercase, one lowercase, one number, one special character. 3) Hash password using bcrypt with appropriate salt rounds. 4) Generate new UUID for user id. 5) Create citizen record for sequential ID via discussion_board_user_citizens. 6) Insert new user record with permission_level='MEMBER', is_banned=false, display_name from request. 7) Create new session record in discussion_board_user_sessions with access_token (15min expiry), refresh_token (7day expiry), and connection metadata. 8) Return tokens and user profile in IAuthorized response.
operations.description:
Registers a new user account on the Economic/Political Discussion Board platform.

The join operation creates a new user account with email and password authentication. The email must be unique across all users in the discussion_board_users table. The password must meet security requirements: minimum 8 characters, at least one uppercase letter, at least one lowercase letter, at least one number, and at least one special character. The password is securely hashed using bcrypt before storage in the password_hash field.

Upon successful registration, the user is assigned MEMBER permission_level, which grants access to create articles, write comments, and manage their own content. A display_name is required and will be shown publicly alongside the user's content and on their profile.

The response includes a JWT access token (valid for 15 minutes) and a refresh token (valid for 7 days), enabling immediate authenticated access without requiring a separate login. The access token contains the user's id, email, and permission_level claims for authorization checks on subsequent API calls.

This is a public endpoint requiring no prior authentication. After registration, users can immediately access all member-level features including article creation, commenting, and profile management.

requestBody.description: User registration information including email, password, and display name.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and user profile information for the newly registered user.

operations.name: join

operations.description:
Authenticates a user with email and password credentials on the Economic/Political Discussion Board.

The login operation validates user credentials against the discussion_board_users table. The email must exist in the system and the password must match the stored password_hash. For security, both invalid email and invalid password return the same generic error message to prevent email enumeration attacks.

Banned users cannot log in. If a user's is_banned flag is true, the authentication is rejected with an error message indicating the account has been banned. The ban reason may be displayed to inform the user of the circumstances.

Successful authentication generates a new session record in discussion_board_user_sessions containing: an access_token (JWT valid for 15 minutes with claims: sub, email, permissionLevel), a refresh_token (JWT valid for 7 days for session renewal), and connection metadata (ip address, href, referrer, user_agent) for security auditing.

The response returns the tokens and user profile information including the permission_level (MEMBER, ADMINISTRATOR, or SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR), which determines the user's access rights within the platform. The permission level is embedded in the JWT for efficient authorization checks on API calls.

This is a public endpoint - no authentication is required to access it. After successful login, the access token should be included in the Authorization header for all authenticated API requests.

operations.specification: Implementation: 1) Extract refresh_token from request body. 2) Validate JWT signature and check token hasn't expired (exp claim vs current time). 3) Verify token type is 'refresh' (type claim). 4) Query discussion_board_user_sessions by refresh_token (unique index lookup) to find the session. 5) If session not found or expired_at < now, return AUTH_REFRESH_FAILED error. 6) Query discussion_board_users by session.discussion_board_user_id to get user record. 7) Check user.is_banned - if true, delete session and return AUTH_USER_BANNED error. 8) Generate new access_token with updated claims (sub, email, current permissionLevel, new 15min exp). 9) Update session.access_token with new token. 10) Return new access_token and existing refresh_token in IAuthorized response.
operations.description:
Renews an expired access token using a valid refresh token for continued authenticated access.

The refresh operation allows users to obtain a new access token without re-entering credentials when their current access token expires (after 15 minutes). The refresh_token from the original login or previous refresh must be provided in the request body.

The system validates the refresh token by: checking the JWT signature and expiration, verifying the token type is 'refresh', looking up the session record in discussion_board_user_sessions by the refresh_token value, and confirming the session has not expired (expired_at field).

Security checks include verifying the user is not banned (is_banned flag in discussion_board_users). If the user has been banned since the session was created, the session is deleted and authentication is denied.

Upon successful validation, a new access_token is generated with the current permission_level from the user record. This ensures that if a user's permissions were changed (promoted to ADMINISTRATOR or demoted), the new token reflects the current authorization level. The refresh_token remains the same, maintaining the session identity.

The response returns the new access_token and the existing refresh_token. The refresh token's expiration (7 days from original login) is not extended - users must re-authenticate with full login after the refresh token expires.

This is a public endpoint - the refresh token itself serves as the authentication credential for this operation.

The access token contains the user's id, email, and permission_level claims for authorization checks on subsequent API calls.

This is a public endpoint requiring no prior authentication. After registration, users can immediately access all member-level features including article creation, commenting, and profile management.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of user profiles on the discussion board platform.

This operation enables users to discover and browse other community members. For regular users, it provides access to public profile information including display names, bios, and membership dates. For administrators, additional filtering capabilities allow searching by ban status and permission level.

The response includes summary profile information optimized for list display. Each user entry contains their display name (or system-generated identifier if not set), a truncated bio preview, permission level, membership date, and ban status indicator for administrators.

Search functionality supports partial matching on display names using trigram-based fuzzy search, enabling users to find others even with approximate spelling. Results can be sorted by creation date (newest or oldest first) with configurable pagination.

Related operations: GET /users/{userId} retrieves detailed profile information including article and comment lists. Administrators may also use GET /admin/banned-users to view the banned user list with ban reasons.
operations.name: index

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for user list retrieval

responseBody.description: Paginated list of user profile summaries

operations.specification:
Query discussion_board_users table with pagination and optional filtering.

DATABASE QUERY:
- SELECT from discussion_board_users WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
- Apply search filters: display_name (ILIKE with trigram for fuzzy match), permission_level (enum filter), is_banned (boolean filter for admins)
- Use GIN index on display_name for trigram search optimization
- Use index on [permission_level, created_at] for filtered sorting
- Use index on [is_banned, created_at] for ban status filtering

PERMISSION CHECK:
- All authenticated users can search and view user profiles
- Ban status filter (is_banned) and permission_level filter restricted to administrators
- Regular users searching with admin-only filters receive empty results or error

PAGINATION:
- Cursor-based pagination using created_at as cursor
- Default page size: 20 users
- Maximum page size: 100 users
- Include total count in pagination metadata

SORTING:
- Default: created_at DESC (newest first)
- Supported: created_at ASC (oldest first)

RESPONSE FIELDS:
- id: User UUID
- display_name: User's display name (required field)
- bio_preview: First 100 characters of bio, null if empty
- permission_level: MEMBER, ADMINISTRATOR, or SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR
- is_banned: Boolean (visible to admins only, hidden for regular users)
- created_at: Account creation timestamp

PERFORMANCE:
- Use trigram index (display_name with gin_trgm_ops) for search
- Consider materialized view for user statistics (article/comment counts) if needed for profile display

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific user's public profile information.

This endpoint returns the user's public profile data, including their display name, biography, and member since date. All registered users can view any other user's profile to learn about the author of articles and comments.

The response includes basic profile information (display_name, bio, member_since) and an activity summary with counts of articles and comments authored by the user. For detailed article and comment lists with pagination, use the dedicated article and comment list endpoints.

If the user has not set a display name, the display_name field will contain a system-generated default identifier. If the user has not provided a bio, the bio field will be null.

Security: This endpoint returns public profile information only. Sensitive fields (email, password) and administrative fields (is_banned, permission_level) are not exposed through this endpoint. The profile remains visible even if the user has been banned; banned status is only visible to administrators through administrative endpoints.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the discussion_board_users table by primary key (id) to retrieve the user record.

The query should:
1. Find the user by UUID primary key (discussion_board_users.id)
2. Include computed fields for activity counts:
   - Article count: COUNT of discussion_board_articles where discussion_board_user_id matches and deleted_at IS NULL
   - Comment count: COUNT of discussion_board_comments where discussion_board_user_id matches and deleted_at IS NULL
3. Return NOT_FOUND (404) if the user does not exist or has been soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NOT NULL)

The response object should map:
- id → user.id
- displayName → user.display_name
- bio → user.bio (can be null)
- memberSince → user.created_at
- articleCount → computed count from discussion_board_articles
- commentCount → computed count from discussion_board_comments

Do NOT include: email, password_hash, permission_level, is_banned, banned_by, citizen_id, updated_at, deleted_at

responseBody.description: User's public profile with basic information and activity summary

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the user whose profile is being retrieved (global scope)

operations.description:
Update the authenticated user's profile information including display name and biography.

This operation allows users to personalize their profile by modifying their display name (visible to other users alongside their content) and an optional biographical text. The display name serves as the primary identifier shown on articles, comments, and profile pages.

**Display Name Validation:**
- Maximum 50 characters
- Allowed characters: letters (A-Z, a-z), numbers (0-9), spaces, hyphens (-), underscores (_), apostrophes (')
- No consecutive spaces allowed
- No leading or trailing spaces
- Display name uniqueness is NOT required - multiple users may have the same display name

**Bio Validation:**
- Maximum 500 characters
- HTML tags and JavaScript code are not permitted
- Line breaks and basic text formatting are preserved
- The bio field is optional and may be null or empty

**Security Considerations:**
- Users can only update their own profile through the authenticated session
- All input is sanitized to prevent HTML/JavaScript injection
- The updated_at timestamp is automatically refreshed upon successful update

**Related Operations:**
- GET /profile/at - Retrieve the authenticated user's own profile
- GET /users/{userId} - View another user's profile

This operation updates the discussion_board_users table record associated with the authenticated user.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update the authenticated user's profile in the discussion_board_users table.

**Implementation Steps:**
1. Extract user ID from the authenticated JWT session context
2. Validate request body:
   - display_name: Check length (1-50 chars), character whitelist (alphanumeric, spaces, hyphens, underscores, apostrophes), no consecutive/leading/trailing spaces
   - bio: Check length (<=500 chars), sanitize HTML/JavaScript tags
3. Execute UPDATE query on discussion_board_users:
   - SET display_name = $displayName, bio = $bio, updated_at = NOW()
   - WHERE id = $authenticatedUserId AND deleted_at IS NULL
4. Return the updated user record

**Validation Rules:**
- Display name regex pattern: ^[a-zA-Z0-9\s\-_']+$ after trimming
- No consecutive spaces: check with regex \s{2,}
- Bio sanitization: strip HTML tags, limit to 500 chars

**Edge Cases:**
- User not found: Return 404 (account may have been deleted)
- Banned user: Allow profile update (ban status doesn't prevent profile management)
- Empty bio: Accept null or empty string
- Partial update: Only update provided fields (display_name and/or bio)

responseBody.description: The updated user profile with modified display name and/or bio

requestBody.description: Profile update data containing the new display name and/or biography

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of user authentication sessions.

This administrative operation provides comprehensive session management capabilities, allowing administrators to monitor active user sessions across the platform. Each session represents an authenticated device or browser instance with associated security metadata.

The response includes session summaries containing the user who owns the session, connection metadata (IP address, browser user agent, referrer URL), and temporal information (creation time, expiration time). This data supports security auditing, fraud detection, and multi-device session management.

Administrators can filter sessions by user ID, creation date range, and expiration status. Results are paginated and can be sorted by creation time to facilitate chronological session tracking. The operation supports identifying suspicious login patterns, managing compromised accounts, and auditing user authentication activity across the discussion board platform.
operations.name: index

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for session filtering

responseBody.description: Paginated list of session summaries with user and connection metadata

operations.specification:
Query discussion_board_user_sessions table with pagination and filtering capabilities.

Apply search filters:
- Filter by discussion_board_user_id to view sessions for a specific user
- Filter by created_at date range to find sessions within a time period
- Filter by expired_at to distinguish active vs expired sessions

Join with discussion_board_users to include user information (email, display_name, permission_level).

Sort options:
- created_at ascending (oldest first)
- created_at descending (newest first, default)

Return paginated results with cursor-based pagination for efficient large dataset handling.

Security considerations:
- Access tokens and refresh tokens should NOT be included in the summary response
- Only include session metadata safe for administrative viewing

Response includes: session id, user info (id, email, display_name), IP address, user agent, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at, and session status (active/expired).

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific user session.

This operation allows authenticated users to view the details of a single session, including the device information (user agent), connection metadata (IP address, href, referrer), and session validity period (created_at, expired_at). Users can only view their own sessions.

The session information is useful for security purposes, allowing users to review which devices have active sessions and identify any suspicious activity. The refresh_token uniquely identifies each session and can be used to terminate the session.

Related operations:
- PATCH /sessions - List all active sessions for the authenticated user
- DELETE /sessions/{sessionId} - Terminate a specific session
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Implementation steps:

1. Extract sessionId from path parameter and validate as UUID format
2. Query discussion_board_user_sessions table by primary key id
3. Verify the session belongs to the authenticated user (match discussion_board_user_id with current user's id)
4. If session not found or doesn't belong to user, return 404 Not Found
5. Return full session entity including:
   - id: Session UUID
   - access_token: Current access token
   - refresh_token: Session identifier
   - ip: IP address from login
   - href: URL where login was initiated
   - referrer: Referrer URL (nullable)
   - user_agent: Browser/device identification (nullable)
   - created_at: Session creation timestamp
   - expired_at: Session expiration timestamp

Security considerations:
- Users can only view their own sessions
- Do not expose sensitive token data beyond what's necessary for session management display
- Consider masking or truncating token values in response if not needed for client functionality

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of administrative action logs for audit and accountability purposes.

This endpoint provides administrators with comprehensive access to the platform's audit trail, recording all administrative actions including content moderation (article/comment deletion), section management (create/edit/delete), user management (ban/unban), admin hierarchy management (promote/demote), and admin request workflow (approve/reject).

Each log entry captures the administrator who performed the action, the action type, the target entity affected, the original content author (for content moderation actions), an optional reason, timestamp, and client metadata (IP address, user agent). Logs are immutable and cannot be modified or deleted, ensuring complete accountability.

The endpoint supports advanced filtering capabilities including action type filtering, target type filtering, administrator identification, date range queries, and full-text search on reason and target title fields. Results are paginated with cursor-based navigation for efficient large dataset handling.

Access is restricted to authenticated administrators (regular administrators and super administrators) only, as defined in the platform's permission hierarchy. Regular users cannot access audit logs.
operations.name: index

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering administrative action logs

responseBody.description: Paginated list of administrative action log entries with summary information

operations.specification:
Query discussion_board_admin_action_logs table with pagination and filtering support.

Implementation steps:
1. Verify the requesting user has administrator or super_administrator permission level
2. Build Prisma query with provided filters:
   - action_type: Filter by administrative action type (ARTICLE_DELETE, COMMENT_DELETE, SECTION_CREATE, SECTION_EDIT, SECTION_DELETE, BAN_USER, UNBAN_USER, PROMOTE_ADMIN, DEMOTE_ADMIN, APPROVE_REQUEST, REJECT_REQUEST)
   - target_type: Filter by entity type (ARTICLE, COMMENT, SECTION, USER, ADMIN_REQUEST)
   - administrator_id: Filter by specific administrator who performed actions
   - original_author_id: Filter by original content author (for content moderation)
   - created_at range: Filter by date range (from/to)
   - search: Full-text search on target_title and reason fields using trigram indexes
3. Join with discussion_board_users for administrator display name and original author display name
4. Apply cursor-based pagination using created_at descending (newest first)
5. Return paginated results with summary fields: id, action_type, target_type, target_id, target_title, administrator display name, original author display name (if applicable), reason, created_at

Edge cases:
- Return empty array if no logs match filters
- Handle deleted user references gracefully (display 'Deleted User' or null)
- Enforce maximum page size (100 entries)
- Validate action_type and target_type against allowed enum values

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific administrative action log entry.

This endpoint provides administrators with comprehensive details about a single administrative action recorded in the audit trail. The response includes the administrator's identity, action type, target entity information, optional reason/notes, IP address, user agent, and timestamp.

Administrative action logs are immutable and serve as the authoritative record for all platform governance activities including content moderation (article/comment deletion), section management, user banning/unbanning, admin hierarchy changes, and admin request reviews.

This operation supports audit and compliance workflows, allowing administrators to investigate specific actions, verify proper conduct, and maintain accountability across all administrative activities.

Access is restricted to authenticated administrators (both regular and super administrators) to ensure sensitive audit information remains protected.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the discussion_board_admin_action_logs table by primary key (id) to retrieve the specific audit log entry.

Include related data via joins:
- Join with discussion_board_users on administrator_id to fetch the administrator's display name
- Left join with discussion_board_users on original_author_id to fetch the original content author's display name (null for actions not involving user-created content)

Return the complete log record with:
- administrator: object with id and display name
- originalAuthor: nullable object with id and display name
- actionType: the type of action performed
- targetType: the entity type affected
- targetId: UUID of the target entity
- targetTitle: human-readable title/preview
- reason: optional notes/reason text
- ip: administrator's IP address at time of action
- userAgent: administrator's client information
- createdAt: timestamp of the action

Return 404 Not Found if the audit log entry does not exist.
Return 403 Forbidden if the requester is not an administrator.

responseBody.description: Detailed administrative action log entry

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the administrative action log entry to retrieve
parameters.name: auditLogId

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of all active discussion board sections.

This endpoint provides public access to browse all available sections on the discussion board. Each section represents a topic category such as Politics, Economy, or Current Affairs, and serves as the primary organizational structure for articles.

The response includes each section's name, description, and the current count of articles within that section. Results are sorted alphabetically by section name to facilitate easy navigation. Soft-deleted sections are automatically excluded from the list.

This endpoint is accessible to all users, including non-authenticated visitors, enabling content discovery without requiring login. For detailed article listings within a specific section, use the article list endpoint with the section identifier.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query discussion_board_sections table with pagination support.

Implementation steps:
1. Filter records where deleted_at IS NULL to exclude soft-deleted sections
2. Apply pagination using standard limit/offset pattern
3. Count articles in each section via discussion_board_articles table (where deleted_at IS NULL on articles as well)
4. Sort results alphabetically by name (case-insensitive)
5. Return paginated response with section summaries

The article count should reflect only active (non-deleted) articles in each section. Use LEFT JOIN with articles table and COUNT aggregation for efficiency. Consider caching section list if frequently accessed.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of section summaries

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific discussion board section.

This endpoint returns comprehensive information about a section identified by its unique UUID identifier. The response includes the section's display name, description, creator and modifier information, article count, and timestamps.

Sections serve as the primary organizational structure for the discussion board, grouping articles by topic categories such as Politics, Economy, and Current Affairs. This endpoint is the entry point for users to explore content within a specific section.

All users, including non-authenticated users, can access this endpoint to browse available discussion topics.

After retrieving section details, clients can use the section ID to fetch the list of articles within that section through a separate articles endpoint with pagination support.

If the specified section does not exist or has been deleted, a 404 Not Found error is returned.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query the discussion_board_sections table by primary key ID with a filter for null deleted_at to exclude soft-deleted sections. Join with discussion_board_users table on creator_id to retrieve creator's display name and profile information. Optionally join on modifier_id if present to retrieve modifier's display name. Count the number of associated articles by querying discussion_board_articles with filter on discussion_board_section_id and null deleted_at (only count active articles). Return 404 Not Found if section does not exist or has been soft-deleted. Map the database result to IDiscussionBoardSection response type including: id (UUID), name (unique string), description (string), creator information (IDiscussionBoardSection.IAuthor with id and displayName), modifier information if exists (IDiscussionBoardSection.IAuthor optional), articleCount (integer), createdAt (timestamp), updatedAt (timestamp).

operations.description:
Create a new discussion board section for organizing articles by topic categories.

This operation allows administrators to create new sections such as Politics, Economy, or Current Affairs. Each section serves as a primary organizational structure for articles, enabling topic-based content discovery.

The section name must be unique across all sections in the system. If a section with the same name already exists, the operation will fail with a validation error.

This operation requires administrator or super administrator privileges. Regular members will receive an authorization error when attempting to create sections.

Upon successful creation, the system automatically records the creating administrator's ID and the current timestamp for audit purposes. The section becomes immediately available for article association and user browsing.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Implementation steps:

1. Validate user authentication and administrator privileges (check user.permission_level is ADMINISTRATOR or SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR)

2. Validate request body:
   - name: required, string, 2-100 characters, trimmed, not whitespace-only
   - description: required, string, 10-500 characters, trimmed, not whitespace-only

3. Check name uniqueness by querying discussion_board_sections where name equals the provided name and deleted_at is null

4. If duplicate name exists, return 409 Conflict error with message indicating name conflict

5. Create new section record:
   - Generate UUID for id
   - Set creator_id to authenticated user's id
   - Set modifier_id to null (no modification yet)
   - Set name and description from request
   - Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp
   - Set deleted_at to null

6. Return the created section with all fields

responseBody.description: The newly created section with all generated and provided fields

requestBody.description: Section creation data including unique name and description

operations.description:
Update an existing discussion board section's name and description.

This operation allows administrators to modify section properties including the section name and description. The section name must be unique across all sections; attempting to use a name that already exists will result in a validation error. Only administrators have permission to perform this operation.

Upon successful update, the system records the administrator who made the modification and updates the timestamp accordingly. All existing articles within the section remain associated with the section under its updated properties.

Related operations:
- POST /sections: Create a new section
- DELETE /sections/{sectionId}: Delete a section
- GET /sections: List all sections
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Implementation steps:

1. Validate user is authenticated and has ADMINISTRATOR or SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR permission level
2. Query discussion_board_sections table to find the section by id
3. Return 404 error if section not found or is soft-deleted (deleted_at is not null)
4. Validate request body:
   - name: required, 2-100 characters, trimmed, unique across all sections (excluding current section)
   - description: required, 10-500 characters, trimmed
5. If new name conflicts with another section, return 400 error with message 'A section with this name already exists.'
6. Update the section record:
   - Set name to new value
   - Set description to new value
   - Set modifier_id to current user's id
   - Set updated_at to current timestamp
7. Return the updated section with all fields including related creator and modifier user references

responseBody.description: The updated section with all properties including modification metadata

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the section to update
parameters.name: sectionId
