operations.description:
Reverses an active user ban, restoring the user's ability to access the platform.

This administrative operation allows administrators and super administrators to lift existing bans on users. The unban action requires providing a reason for the reversal (10-1000 characters), which is recorded for audit and transparency purposes.

The operation validates that the target ban record exists and has not already been reversed. Upon successful unban, the `is_banned` field in the `discussion_board_users` table is set to `false`, restoring the user's ability to log in and participate in the platform. The original ban record and all related content remain intact for historical reference.

Authorization follows the administrative hierarchy: regular administrators can unban users they banned or users banned by lower-level administrators, while super administrators can unban any user.

Related operations: GET /bans (list banned users), POST /bans (create ban), GET /bans/{banId}/history (view ban history).
operations.name: create

requestBody.description: Unban creation details including the ban record to reverse and the reason for unban action

responseBody.description: The created unban record with full details including timestamps and administrator reference

operations.specification:
Implementation steps for unban creation:

1. AUTHORIZATION CHECK: Verify the authenticated user has administrator or super administrator permission level. Extract administrator_id from the JWT session token.

2. INPUT VALIDATION:
   - Validate discussion_board_ban_id exists in discussion_board_bans table
   - Validate reason is between 10-1000 characters
   - Check that no existing unban record exists for this ban_id (discussion_board_unbans.discussion_board_ban_id is unique)

3. HIERARCHY CHECK (if applicable):
   - For regular administrators: verify they can unban users banned by same or lower-level administrators
   - Super administrators bypass hierarchy restrictions

4. CREATE UNBAN RECORD:
   - Insert new record into discussion_board_unbans with:
     - discussion_board_ban_id (from request)
     - administrator_id (from authenticated session)
     - reason (from request)
     - created_at and updated_at (current timestamp)
   - Handle potential race condition with unique constraint on discussion_board_ban_id

5. USER STATUS UPDATE:
   - The user's active ban status is determined by checking if an unban record exists for their ban
   - No direct status field update needed - status is derived from ban/unban relationship

6. AUDIT LOG: Create entry in discussion_board_ban_histories for audit trail (action: UNBAN)

7. RETURN the created unban record joined with related ban and administrator information

ERROR HANDLING:
- 404 if ban record not found
- 400 if ban already has an unban (USER_NOT_BANNED or already unbanned)
- 403 if administrator lacks permission to unban this user
- 400 if validation fails (BAN_REASON_REQUIRED, BAN_REASON_TOO_LONG)

prerequisites.description: A ban record must exist before it can be reversed by an unban action. The discussion_board_ban_id in the unban request references an existing ban record created by this operation.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of ban and unban administrative action records from the audit trail.

This endpoint provides administrators with comprehensive access to the immutable audit history of all user ban and unban actions performed on the platform. Each record captures the complete context of the administrative action, including the affected user, the administrator who performed the action, the reason provided, and the timestamp.

**Authorization**: Only administrators (both regular and super administrators) can access this endpoint. Regular users cannot view ban history records.

**Audit Trail Contents**:
- BAN actions: Records when a user was banned from the platform
- UNBAN actions: Records when a previously banned user had their access restored

**Filtering Capabilities**:
- Action type: Filter to show only BAN or UNBAN actions
- Administrator: Filter by the administrator who performed the actions
- Target user: Filter by the user who was banned or unbanned
- Date range: Filter by when the actions occurred

**Compliance and Transparency**:
Records in this audit trail are immutable and persist even when referenced users or ban records are deleted, supporting compliance requirements and administrative accountability.

**Related Endpoints**:
- GET /ban-histories/{banHistoryId}: Retrieve detailed information about a specific audit record
- PATCH /bans: List currently banned users
- GET /users/{userId}: View user profile including ban status
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the discussion_board_ban_histories table with pagination and filtering support.

**Database Query Logic**:
1. Apply filters from request body:
   - action_type: Exact match on action_type column ('BAN' or 'UNBAN')
   - actor_id: Exact match on actor_id column (administrator who performed action)
   - discussion_board_user_id: Exact match on target user
   - created_at range: Filter on created_at column using from/to timestamps

2. Include related entities via joins:
   - Join discussion_board_users for target user details (discussion_board_user_id)
   - Join discussion_board_users for actor details (actor_id)
   - Left join discussion_board_bans for ban record reference (discussion_board_ban_id)

3. Sort by created_at descending (most recent actions first) as per FR-LIST-004

4. Apply pagination using cursor-based approach with configurable page size (default 20, max 100)

**Response Construction**:
- Return IDiscussionBoardBanHistory.ISummary for each record
- Include actor's display name and email
- Include target user's display name and email
- Handle null user references gracefully (for deleted users, FR-AUDIT-005)

**Performance Considerations**:
- Use index on created_at for sorting
- Use index on action_type for filtering
- Use composite index on (actor_id, created_at) for administrator filtering
- Use composite index on (discussion_board_user_id, created_at) for target user filtering

responseBody.description: Paginated list of ban and unban history records

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering ban history records

operations.description:
Retrieves a specific ban history audit record by its unique identifier.

This operation provides administrators with detailed information about a single ban or unban action recorded in the audit trail. Each ban history record captures the complete context of the administrative action including the affected user (target user), the administrator who performed the action (actor), the type of action performed (BAN or UNBAN), the reason text provided for the action, and the timestamp when the action occurred.

The response includes embedded information about the target user and the administrator actor, allowing administrators to understand the full context of the action without making additional API calls. For UNBAN actions, the record may also reference the original ban record through the banId field.

This endpoint is part of the compliance-focused audit system. Records are immutable and persist even if the referenced users or ban records are deleted, ensuring a complete audit trail for administrative accountability.

Only users with administrator privileges can access this endpoint. The operation supports filtering by action type for reporting, filtering by administrator for accountability tracking, and filtering by date range for compliance audits when used in conjunction with the ban history list endpoint.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the discussion_board_ban_histories table by primary key (id) to retrieve a single ban history audit record.

Implementation steps:
1. Validate banHistoryId path parameter as valid UUID format
2. Query discussion_board_ban_histories where id = banHistoryId
3. Join with discussion_board_users for targetUser (discussion_board_user_id) - may be null if user was deleted
4. Join with discussion_board_users for actor (actor_id) - may be null if admin was deleted
5. Optionally join with discussion_board_bans for the original ban record reference
6. Return 404 NOT_FOUND if no record exists with the provided ID
7. Return the complete ban history record with embedded user summaries

Response includes:
- id: UUID primary key
- actionType: 'BAN' or 'UNBAN'
- reason: Text reason (10-1000 characters)
- createdAt: Timestamp of action
- targetUser: User summary (id, displayName, email) or null if deleted
- actor: Administrator summary (id, displayName) or null if deleted
- banId: Reference to original ban record (for UNBAN actions) or null

Error handling:
- 401 UNAUTHORIZED if not authenticated
- 403 FORBIDDEN if not an administrator
- 404 NOT_FOUND if ban history record does not exist

responseBody.description: The requested ban history audit record with target user and actor information

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the ban history audit record to retrieve
parameters.name: banHistoryId

operations.description:
Search for articles across all sections by matching text in the title or content fields of the discussion_board_articles table.

This operation provides full-text search capabilities across the entire discussion board, enabling users to discover articles containing specific keywords or phrases. The search scans both article titles and content bodies for matches, returning a paginated list of matching articles with summary information.

Results can be filtered by one or more tags using OR logic - articles matching ANY of the specified tags will be included in results. Tag filtering is implemented through the discussion_board_article_tags junction table, which links articles to entries in the discussion_board_tags master table. When combining search query with tag filters, articles must match the search text AND have at least one of the specified tags.

The search requires a minimum of 2 characters in the query string to prevent overly broad results. Results are sorted by the created_at timestamp from discussion_board_articles, either newest first (default) or oldest first, and are paginated with a maximum of 20 articles per page.

Each result entry includes the article title, author display name from discussion_board_users, associated tags from discussion_board_tags, comment count from discussion_board_comments (excluding soft-deleted comments), and posting timestamp. Clicking on a result navigates to the full article detail view. Empty results display an appropriate message with suggestions for refining the search query.

Public access is granted to all users including guests, allowing content discovery without authentication requirements. The operation respects soft-deletion status by excluding articles where the deleted_at field is set.
operations.name: search
operations.specification:
Implement full-text search on discussion_board_articles table using PostgreSQL full-text search capabilities on title and content columns.

Query construction:
1. Filter articles where deleted_at IS NULL to exclude soft-deleted content
2. Apply full-text search using PostgreSQL tsvector on title and content
3. If tag filters provided, join discussion_board_article_tags and discussion_board_tags to filter by tag values (OR logic)
4. Apply sorting by created_at (DESC for newest, ASC for oldest)
5. Apply pagination using LIMIT/OFFSET based on request parameters

Database queries:
- Use LEFT JOIN with discussion_board_users for author display_name
- Use LEFT JOIN with discussion_board_article_tags and discussion_board_tags for tag aggregation
- Use subquery to count comments per article from discussion_board_comments where deleted_at IS NULL

Performance considerations:
- Add GIN index on title column for trigram search (already exists per schema)
- Consider caching popular search queries
- Return results within 2 seconds as per non-functional requirements

Validation:
- Minimum query length: 2 characters (return validation error if shorter)
- Maximum page size: 20 items
- Default sort: newest first (created_at DESC)

responseBody.description: Paginated list of articles matching the search criteria

requestBody.description: Search criteria including query text, pagination, sorting, and tag filters

operations.description:
Approve a pending administrator request, granting the requester regular administrator status.

This operation allows super administrators to review and approve administrator requests submitted by users seeking administrative privileges. Upon approval, the requester's account is updated from MEMBER to ADMINISTRATOR permission level, enabling them to perform moderation tasks, manage sections, and ban users.

The approval process updates the admin request record by setting the status to 'approved', recording the reviewer's identity, capturing the reviewed_at timestamp, and storing any optional review notes. An audit log entry is created in discussion_board_admin_action_logs with action_type APPROVE_REQUEST to maintain accountability.

This operation enforces authorization constraints: only users with SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR permission level may approve requests. The target request must exist and have a status of 'pending'. Attempting to approve a request that has already been approved or rejected will result in an error. Super administrators cannot approve their own requests as they are already administrators.

Related operations: GET /adminRequests (list pending requests), POST /adminRequests/{adminRequestId}/reject (reject request).
operations.name: approve
operations.specification:
Implementation steps:

1. Authenticate and verify the current user has SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR permission level
2. Validate the adminRequestId parameter (must be valid UUID)
3. Query discussion_board_admin_requests table to find the target request by id
4. Verify the request exists and has status 'pending'
5. Verify the requester is not the current user (self-approval prevention)
6. Verify the requester is not already an administrator
7. Create a database transaction:
   a. Update discussion_board_admin_requests: set status='approved', reviewer_id=current_user.id, reviewed_at=now(), review_notes=provided_notes, updated_at=now()
   b. Update discussion_board_users: set permission_level='ADMINISTRATOR' where id=request.requester_id
   c. Create discussion_board_admin_action_logs entry: administrator_id=current_user.id, original_author_id=request.requester_id, action_type='APPROVE_REQUEST', target_type='ADMIN_REQUEST', target_id=request.id, target_title=requester.display_name, reason=review_notes, ip=request.ip, user_agent=request.user_agent, created_at=now()
8. Commit the transaction
9. Return the updated admin request with populated requester and reviewer relations

Error handling:
- 401 Unauthorized: User not authenticated
- 403 Forbidden: User is not a super administrator
- 404 Not Found: Admin request not found
- 409 Conflict: Request already processed (not pending)
- 409 Conflict: Requester is already an administrator
- 409 Conflict: Self-approval attempt

responseBody.description: The approved administrator request with updated status, reviewer information, and approval timestamp

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the administrator request to approve (global scope)
parameters.name: adminRequestId

requestBody.description: Optional review notes explaining the approval decision

operations.description:
Rejects a pending administrator request.

This endpoint allows super administrators to reject user requests to become administrators. When a request is rejected, its status changes from 'pending' to 'rejected', and the requesting user is not granted administrative privileges.

The operation is restricted to super administrators only. Regular administrators and regular users cannot access this endpoint. The admin request must exist and be in 'pending' status to be rejected. Attempting to reject an already processed (approved or rejected) request will result in an error.

This operation is part of the administrator management workflow, which includes viewing pending requests, approving requests, and managing the admin hierarchy. Each rejection is logged in the admin action logs for audit purposes.
operations.name: reject

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the admin request to reject. The request must exist and be in 'pending' status.
parameters.name: adminRequestId

responseBody.description: The rejected admin request with updated status and review information

operations.specification:
Implementation steps:

1. Authenticate the requesting user and verify they have SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR permission level
2. Validate adminRequestId parameter exists and is a valid UUID
3. Query discussion_board_admin_requests table to find the request by ID
4. Verify the request exists and is in 'pending' status (cannot reject already processed requests)
5. Update the request record:
   - Set status to 'rejected'
   - Set reviewed_at to current timestamp
   - Set reviewed_by to the current super administrator's user ID
6. Create an audit log entry in discussion_board_admin_action_logs for this rejection action
7. Return the updated admin request object

Error conditions:
- 401 Unauthorized: User not authenticated
- 403 Forbidden: User is not a super administrator
- 404 Not Found: Admin request does not exist
- 409 Conflict: Request is already approved or rejected

Database tables involved:
- discussion_board_admin_requests: Update status, reviewed_at, reviewed_by
- discussion_board_admin_action_logs: Create audit record
- discussion_board_users: Verify admin permissions

prerequisites.description: Admin request must exist and be in 'pending' status before it can be rejected. This operation creates the admin request that will be rejected.

operations.description:
Promote a regular administrator to super administrator status.

This operation allows super administrators to elevate regular administrators to the highest permission level in the platform hierarchy. Upon successful promotion, the target user gains all super administrator privileges including the ability to review and approve administrator requests, and to promote or demote other administrators.

The promotion process includes several validation steps: the caller must be a super administrator, the target user must currently be a regular administrator (not a regular member or already a super administrator), and the target user must not be banned. If any of these conditions are not met, the operation will fail with an appropriate error message.

All promotion actions are recorded in the audit trail (discussion_board_admin_hierarchy_actions table) with the actor's identity, target's identity, action type 'PROMOTION', optional reason, and timestamp. This ensures accountability and enables historical tracking of all hierarchy changes.

Related operations: Use POST /administrators/{administratorId}/demote to reverse this action (demote a super administrator to regular administrator). Use PATCH /administrators to list administrators and their current permission levels.
operations.name: promote
operations.specification:
Implement promotion workflow:

1. Authentication & Authorization:
   - Verify caller is authenticated
   - Verify caller has SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR permission_level
   - Return 403 Forbidden if caller is not a super administrator

2. Target Validation:
   - Query discussion_board_users by administratorId path parameter
   - Return 404 Not Found if user does not exist
   - Verify target's permission_level is 'ADMINISTRATOR' (not MEMBER or SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR)
   - Return 400 Bad Request if target is not a regular administrator
   - Verify target's is_banned is false
   - Return 400 Bad Request if target is banned

3. Self-Promotion Prevention:
   - Verify administratorId does not match caller's user ID
   - Return 400 Bad Request if attempting self-promotion

4. Execute Promotion:
   - Update target user's permission_level to 'SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR'
   - Update target user's updated_at timestamp

5. Create Audit Record:
   - Insert record into discussion_board_admin_hierarchy_actions:
     - actor_id: caller's user ID
     - target_id: administratorId
     - action_type: 'PROMOTION'
     - reason: optional reason from request body (or null)
     - created_at: current timestamp

6. Return Response:
   - Return updated user object with new permission level

7. Send Notification:
   - Trigger notification to promoted user about their elevation

responseBody.description: The updated administrator with super administrator status

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the regular administrator to be promoted to super administrator status
parameters.name: administratorId

requestBody.description: Promotion details including optional reason for the promotion

prerequisites.description: Admin request must be submitted for the user before it can be approved to grant administrator privileges
Admin request approval grants ADMINISTRATOR permission level, making the user eligible for promotion to super administrator

operations.description:
Demotes a super administrator to regular administrator status.

This operation allows a super administrator to downgrade another super administrator's permission level from SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR to ADMINISTRATOR. The demotion is recorded in the admin hierarchy audit trail for compliance purposes.

**Authorization Requirements**: Only super administrators can perform this operation.

**Business Rules**:
- The target user must currently be a super administrator
- A super administrator cannot demote themselves (self-protection mechanism)
- At least one super administrator must remain in the system after demotion
- The demotion takes effect immediately upon successful execution

**Audit Trail**: The operation creates an immutable record in the admin_hierarchy_actions table containing the actor's ID, target's ID, action type 'DEMOTION', optional reason, and timestamp.

**Related Operations**: After demotion, the affected user retains regular administrator privileges. To restore super administrator status, use the promote operation (POST /administrators/{administratorId}/promote).
operations.name: demote
operations.specification:
Implementation steps:

1. **Authorization Check**: Verify the authenticated user has SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR permission_level in discussion_board_users table.

2. **Target Validation**:
   - Query discussion_board_users to find the target administrator by administratorId
   - Verify target exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL)
   - Verify target's permission_level equals 'SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR'
   - Verify target's id does not match the actor's id (prevent self-demotion)

3. **Last Super Admin Check**:
   - Count users with permission_level = 'SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR' and is_banned = false and deleted_at IS NULL
   - If count would be zero after demotion, reject with appropriate error

4. **Execute Demotion**:
   - Update target's permission_level to 'ADMINISTRATOR' in discussion_board_users
   - Update target's updated_at timestamp

5. **Create Audit Record**:
   - Insert record into discussion_board_admin_hierarchy_actions with:
     - actor_id: current authenticated user's id
     - target_id: the demoted administrator's id
     - action_type: 'DEMOTION'
     - reason: from request body (may be null)
     - created_at: current timestamp

6. **Return Response**: Return the updated user object with new ADMINISTRATOR permission level.

**Error Handling**:
- 401 Unauthorized: User not authenticated
- 403 Forbidden: User is not a super administrator
- 404 Not Found: Target administrator does not exist
- 400 Bad Request: Target is not a super administrator
- 400 Bad Request: Self-demotion attempt
- 400 Bad Request: Would result in zero super administrators

responseBody.description: The demoted administrator with updated permission level

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the super administrator to demote to regular administrator status
parameters.name: administratorId

requestBody.description: Demotion details including optional reason for the action

operations.description:
Retrieves the current ban status for a specific user, including whether the user is banned and, if applicable, the ban details such as reason, administrator who performed the ban, and timestamp.

This operation is primarily used by administrators to check user ban status for moderation purposes. The response includes the user's banned state and, when banned, provides the ban reason recorded at the time of the ban action.

The ban status is determined by checking the is_banned field on the user record from the discussion_board_users table. If the user is currently banned, the operation retrieves the most recent active ban record from the discussion_board_bans table, which contains the reason (10-1000 characters), the administrator reference who performed the ban, and the creation timestamp.

This endpoint supports the administrative workflow for user management, enabling administrators to quickly verify ban status before taking further moderation actions or responding to user inquiries.
operations.name: at

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the user whose ban status is being retrieved (UUID format, global scope).
parameters.name: userId

responseBody.description: The ban status information including whether the user is banned and, if applicable, the ban details with reason, administrator, and timestamp.

operations.specification:
Query the discussion_board_users table to retrieve the user record and check the is_banned boolean field. If the user does not exist, return 404 NOT_FOUND error.

If is_banned is false, return a response indicating the user is not banned with minimal data.

If is_banned is true, perform a secondary query on discussion_board_bans table to retrieve the most recent ban record for this user:
- Filter by discussion_board_user_id matching the path parameter
- Order by created_at descending
- Take the first (most recent) record
- Join with discussion_board_users to get administrator display_name

The response should include:
- is_banned: boolean (true)
- reason: string (the ban reason text)
- banned_by: object with administrator id and display_name
- banned_at: DateTime (created_at from ban record)

Performance consideration: Consider adding an index on discussion_board_bans(discussion_board_user_id, created_at desc) for efficient lookup of the most recent ban. This index already exists per schema.

Authorization: Only users with ADMINISTRATOR or SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR permission level can access this endpoint. Regular users (MEMBER) should receive 403 FORBIDDEN.

Retrieve a paginated list of ban and unban history records for a specific user.

This endpoint provides administrators with comprehensive visibility into the moderation actions taken against a user. Each history entry captures whether the action was a ban or unban, the administrator who performed the action, the reason provided, and the timestamp.

The discussion_board_ban_histories table maintains an immutable audit trail as specified in FR-AUDIT-001. Records persist even after users are deleted or unbanned, ensuring compliance and administrative accountability.

Administrators can filter the history by action type (BAN or UNBAN) to focus on specific types of moderation actions. Date range filtering supports compliance audits and historical analysis. Results are sorted by creation timestamp in descending order, showing the most recent actions first.

This operation supports FR-AUDIT-002 which requires displaying ban/unban history when administrators view a user's profile.

Permission levels include: regular member (no admin rights), administrator (can manage sections, moderate content, ban users), and super administrator (can manage admin hierarchy and approve admin requests). Admin permission level is stored as user attribute rather than separate actor type since all users share identical authentication flow.

Indicates which page of results is currently being returned. Page

reflects the page parameter from the request after validation and bounds

statistics.

alongside paginated list data. It enables clients to implement navigation

access.description:
Short-lived JWT access token for authenticating API requests.

This token must be included in the Authorization header using the Bearer
scheme (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer {access}`) for all endpoints requiring
authentication. The token contains encoded claims including user identity,
roles, and permissions. Typically expires within 15-60 minutes for
security; use the refresh token to obtain a new access token when expired.
access.x-autobe-specification: JWT access token. Use in Authorization header as "Bearer {access}".

refresh.description:
Long-lived refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

Used to request new access tokens when the current access token expires,
allowing session continuation without re-authentication. Should be stored
securely and transmitted only to the token refresh endpoint. Typical
lifetime ranges from 7 to 30 days depending on security requirements.
refresh.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens without re-authentication.

expired_at.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the access token expires.

After this timestamp, the access token will be rejected by authenticated
endpoints. Clients should proactively refresh before expiration to maintain
seamless user experience. A common strategy is to refresh when remaining
time falls below 5 minutes. This timestamp is also embedded within the JWT
itself as the "exp" claim.
expired_at.x-autobe-specification: Access token expiration timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

refreshable_until.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp indicating the absolute session expiration deadline.

Represents the latest possible time the refresh token can be used. Once
this timestamp is reached, the user must fully re-authenticate with
credentials. This defines the maximum session duration regardless of
activity. If refresh token rotation is enabled, this deadline may extend
with each successful refresh.
refreshable_until.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token expiration timestamp. Re-authentication required after this time.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
JWT-based authorization token pair with expiration metadata.

Provides a complete authentication token structure containing both access and
refresh tokens along with their respective expiration timestamps. This
dual-token pattern enables secure, stateless authentication with automatic
session renewal capabilities.

The access token is short-lived for security, while the refresh token allows
obtaining new access tokens without requiring the user to re-enter
credentials. This structure is automatically included in authentication
responses across all generated backend applications.
IAuthorizationToken.x-autobe-specification: Dual-token authentication structure with access/refresh tokens and expiration info.

page.x-autobe-specification: Calculates SQL OFFSET as (page - 1) * limit. Default value: 1. Minimum: 1. Used with limit for standard LIMIT/OFFSET pagination. If page exceeds total pages, returns empty result set with correct pagination metadata.

limit.description: Maximum number of tags to return per page. Defaults to 20, maximum allowed is 100. Use lower values for faster responses on large datasets.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Passed directly to SQL LIMIT clause to restrict rows returned per page. Default: 20, Maximum: 100. If limit > 100, clamp to 100. If limit <= 0, use default 20. Lower values improve response time for large tag sets.

IDiscussionBoardTag.IRequest.description: Request parameters for retrieving a paginated list of tags with optional search filtering. Supports case-insensitive partial matching on tag values via the search parameter, and standard pagination controls via page number and items-per-page limit. All parameters are optional—omitting them returns all tags with default pagination (page 1, limit 20).
IDiscussionBoardTag.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: Request DTO for paginated tag listing endpoint PATCH /discussionBoard/tags. Contains query parameters for filtering and pagination: (1) search - applies case-insensitive ILIKE filter on discussion_board_tags.value column for partial matching, (2) page - calculates SQL OFFSET as (page - 1) * limit, defaults to 1, (3) limit - restricts rows via SQL LIMIT clause, defaults to 20, max 100. All parameters optional. Implementation: SELECT id, value FROM discussion_board_tags WHERE value ILIKE '%' || search || '%' ORDER BY value ASC LIMIT $limit OFFSET $offset.

limit.description: Maximum number of articles to return per page. Must be between 1 and 100. Defaults to 20 if not specified.
limit.x-autobe-specification: SQL LIMIT clause. Maximum 100 records per page. Default: 20. Used with OFFSET for pagination: OFFSET = (page-1)*limit. Applied to discussion_board_articles query results.

page.description: Page number to retrieve, starting from 1. Defaults to 1 if not specified.
page.x-autobe-specification: 1-indexed page number for pagination. Converted to OFFSET: OFFSET = (page-1)*limit. Default: 1 (first page). Must be >= 1. Used with limit for standard LIMIT/OFFSET pagination pattern on discussion_board_articles query.

search.description: Search text to find articles matching the query in title or content. Case-insensitive partial matching. Minimum 2 characters required.
search.x-autobe-specification: Full-text search query. Applied as ILIKE pattern match on discussion_board_articles.title OR discussion_board_articles.content columns. Case-insensitive partial matching. Minimum 2 characters required to prevent overly broad results. Empty or short queries return validation error.

sectionId.description: Filter articles by section. Provide the section's UUID to return only articles in that section.
sectionId.x-autobe-specification: Exact match filter on discussion_board_articles.discussion_board_section_id foreign key column. References discussion_board_sections.id. When provided, returns only articles in the specified section. Must be valid UUID format.

sort.description: Sort order for articles. Use 'newest' for most recent first, 'oldest' for earliest first.
sort.x-autobe-specification: Sort direction for results. Maps to ORDER BY discussion_board_articles.created_at ASC (oldest first) or DESC (newest first). Required field. Default behavior when not specified would be newest first (DESC).

tags.description: Filter articles by tags. Provide one or more tag names to return articles containing any of those tags. Uses OR logic - articles matching any tag will be included.
tags.x-autobe-specification: Tag filter for articles. JOINs discussion_board_article_tags junction table to discussion_board_tags master table. Filters articles that have ANY of the specified tags (OR logic). Tags are case-insensitive (normalized to lowercase in DB). Returns articles with at least one matching tag.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.IRequest.description: Request parameters for retrieving a paginated, searchable, and filterable list of discussion board articles. Supports full-text search across title and content, filtering by section and tags, sorting by creation time, and standard pagination controls.
IDiscussionBoardArticle.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: Query parameters for paginated article listing and search. Implementation: WHERE deleted_at IS NULL always applied. search: ILIKE pattern match on discussion_board_articles.title OR discussion_board_articles.content columns. sectionId: exact match filter on discussion_board_articles.discussion_board_section_id foreign key. tags: JOIN through discussion_board_article_tags junction to discussion_board_tags, filter by tag value with OR logic. sort: ORDER BY created_at DESC (newest) or ASC (oldest). page: OFFSET = (page-1)*limit. limit: LIMIT clause with max 100. Defaults: page=1, limit=20, sort=newest. Minimum search length: 2 characters for performance.

displayName.description: Search text for filtering users by display name. Supports partial matching - users with names containing the provided text will be included in results.
displayName.x-autobe-specification: Case-insensitive partial match filter referencing discussion_board_users.display_name column. Uses GIN trigram index (gin_trgm_ops) for efficient fuzzy text search. Query: WHERE display_name ILIKE '%{displayName}%'

email.description: Search text for filtering users by email address. Supports partial matching for finding users with email addresses containing the provided text.
email.x-autobe-specification: Case-insensitive partial match filter referencing discussion_board_users.email column. Query: WHERE email ILIKE '%{email}%'

permissionLevel.description: Filter users by permission level. Valid values: MEMBER (regular user), ADMINISTRATOR, or SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR. This filter is restricted to administrators only.
permissionLevel.x-autobe-specification: Exact match filter referencing discussion_board_users.permission_level column. Valid values: 'MEMBER', 'ADMINISTRATOR', 'SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR'. Query: WHERE permission_level = {permissionLevel}. Admin-only filter - regular users receive error when using this parameter.

isBanned.description: Filter users by ban status. Set to true to see only banned users, false to see only active users. This filter is restricted to administrators only.
isBanned.x-autobe-specification: Boolean filter referencing discussion_board_users.is_banned column. true = only banned users, false = only active users. Query: WHERE is_banned = {isBanned}. Admin-only filter - regular users receive error when using this parameter.

page.description: Page number for paginated results. Starts at 1 for the first page. Use with limit to navigate through result pages.
page.x-autobe-specification: 1-based page number for pagination. Controls OFFSET calculation: OFFSET = (page - 1) * limit. Default: 1. Must be >= 1. Combined with limit to determine result window.

limit.description: Maximum number of user profiles to return per page. Default is 20, maximum is 100. Use with page for pagination control.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum number of records per page. Controls LIMIT clause in query. Default: 20. Maximum: 100. Must be >= 1 and <= 100. Combined with page to determine result window.

IDiscussionBoardUser.IRequest.description: Search and filter parameters for retrieving a paginated list of user profiles. Supports partial text matching on display name and email, filtering by permission level and ban status, and standard pagination controls. All parameters are optional and can be combined for refined searches.
IDiscussionBoardUser.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: Request DTO for searching and filtering user profiles. Properties serve as query parameters for WHERE clause construction and OFFSET/LIMIT pagination against discussion_board_users table. Filter parameters reference DB columns: displayName→display_name (ILIKE), email→email (ILIKE), permissionLevel→permission_level (exact), isBanned→is_banned (exact). Pagination parameters (page, limit) control result windowing. All parameters optional. Used by PATCH /discussionBoard/users endpoint.

id.description: Unique identifier for the unban record.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_unbans.id. Auto-generated UUID primary key.

ban.description: The original ban record that this unban action reverses.
ban.x-autobe-specification: JOIN via discussion_board_ban_id foreign key to discussion_board_bans.id. Returns full IDiscussionBoardBan entity containing the original ban record details including the banned user, ban reason, and the administrator who performed the ban.

administrator.description: The administrator who performed the unban action.
administrator.x-autobe-specification: JOIN via administrator_id foreign key to discussion_board_users.id. Returns IDiscussionBoardUser.ISummary containing id, displayName, and email of the administrator who performed the unban action.

reason.description: The documented reason for lifting the ban, recorded for transparency and audit purposes.
reason.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_unbans.reason. Text field validated to be between 10 and 1000 characters. Records the administrative justification for reversing the ban.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the unban action was recorded.
createdAt.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_unbans.created_at. ISO 8601 timestamp of when the unban action was performed.

IDiscussionBoardUnban.description: Unban record representing the reversal of an active user ban. Contains the original ban record being reversed, the administrator who performed the unban action, the documented reason for the reversal, and the creation timestamp. Unban records maintain a complete audit trail of ban removal decisions for administrative accountability and compliance purposes.
IDiscussionBoardUnban.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_unbans table. Primary key: id (UUID). Columns: reason (text, validated 10-1000 chars), created_at (timestamp). Relations: ban (JOIN via discussion_board_ban_id FK to discussion_board_bans.id, returns IDiscussionBoardBan entity), administrator (JOIN via administrator_id FK to discussion_board_users.id, returns IDiscussionBoardUser.ISummary). Raw FK columns (discussion_board_ban_id, administrator_id) excluded in favor of nested objects. Soft-delete and update tracking columns (deleted_at, updated_at) excluded as internal fields.

value.description: Tag value to associate with the article. The value will be normalized to lowercase and matched to an existing platform tag or used to create a new one automatically. Supports alphanumeric characters, hyphens, and underscores only.
value.x-autobe-specification: User-provided tag text input. Processing pipeline: 1) Trim leading/trailing whitespace, 2) Validate length (1-50 characters), 3) Validate characters (alphanumeric, hyphens, underscores only), 4) Normalize to lowercase for case-insensitive comparison, 5) Lookup in discussion_board_tags table by unique value constraint, 6) Create new tag record in discussion_board_tags if not found, 7) Create association in discussion_board_article_tags linking article to tag. Does not map directly to any discussion_board_article_tags column.

IDiscussionBoardArticleTag.ICreate.description: Request body for adding tags to an article. Contains the tag value to associate with the article. The tag value is automatically normalized to lowercase and will reference an existing platform tag or create a new one automatically.
IDiscussionBoardArticleTag.ICreate.x-autobe-specification: Transformation DTO for article-tag association. The value field receives user-provided tag text, which is normalized (trimmed, lowercased), validated (1-50 characters, alphanumeric/hyphens/underscores only), then used to lookup or create a record in discussion_board_tags. The resulting tag ID is linked to the article via discussion_board_article_tags junction table. Article ID is sourced from the path parameter {articleId}, not the request body. Maximum 15 tags per article enforced at application layer.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user account.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_users.id. UUID format generated by database.

displayName.description: User's display name shown on their profile and alongside their content. Visible to other users.
displayName.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_users.display_name. Transform snake_case to camelCase.

email.description: User's primary email address used for authentication.
email.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_users.email. Used for authentication and identification.

IDiscussionBoardUser.ISummary.description: Lightweight user profile summary for display in lists, article authors, comment authors, and administrative records. Contains essential identification (id, email) and display name without exposing sensitive data or detailed activity information. Used across public contexts (viewing article/comment authors) and administrative contexts (ban records, admin action audit trails, request workflows).
IDiscussionBoardUser.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_users table for summary display. Query columns: id, display_name, email. Transform snake_case to camelCase: display_name → displayName. Exclude sensitive field password_hash and detailed profile fields. This summary is used for user display in article authors, comment authors, admin action logs, ban records, admin request requesters/reviewers, session user references, and hierarchy action actors/targets. No JOINs required for ISummary fields.

IDiscussionBoardBanHistory.ISummary.description: Lightweight summary of a ban or unban action record for audit trail list display. Captures essential information for administrative review: the action type, target user, administrator who performed the action, reason for transparency, and timestamp.
IDiscussionBoardBanHistory.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_ban_histories table with relation joins for user summaries. Query selects: id, action_type, reason, created_at from discussion_board_ban_histories. Joins discussion_board_users twice via discussion_board_user_id and actor_id to populate targetUser and actor summaries. Both user references may be null in database (for deleted users per FR-AUDIT-005) but returned as nullable ISummary in response. Sort order is handled by parent query.

reviewNotes.description: Optional notes from the super administrator explaining the approval decision. Provides context for audit trails and administrative transparency.
reviewNotes.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to discussion_board_admin_requests.review_notes column. Optional text field allowing the super administrator to document the rationale for approving the request. Stored as nullable VARCHAR in database. If null, the approval proceeds without explanatory notes.

IDiscussionBoardAdminRequest.IApprove.description: Request body for approving a pending administrator request. Contains optional review notes from the super administrator explaining the approval decision. The administrator request ID is provided in the URL path, and the reviewer's identity is automatically obtained from the authentication token.
IDiscussionBoardAdminRequest.IApprove.x-autobe-specification: Request body for the admin request approval operation. The reviewNotes field maps directly to the review_notes column in discussion_board_admin_requests table. Upon approval, the system automatically sets: status='approved', reviewer_id from JWT authentication context, reviewed_at to current timestamp, updated_at to current timestamp. The id is provided via path parameter, and requester_id/reason are preserved from the existing request record. The reviewer relation is populated from the authenticated super administrator's user record.

limit.description: Maximum number of comments to return per page. Accepts values from 1 to 100. Defaults to 20 when not specified.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Pagination parameter controlling maximum records per page. Maps to SQL LIMIT clause. Value range: 1-100 (enforced by minimum/maximum constraints). Used in OFFSET calculation: LIMIT = limit. Default: 20 when null. Capped at 100 to prevent excessive result sets.

page.description: Page number to retrieve, starting from 1. Defaults to 1 when not specified. Use together with limit to navigate through results.
page.x-autobe-specification: Pagination parameter for page navigation. 1-indexed page number used to calculate SQL OFFSET: OFFSET = (page - 1) * limit. Default: 1 (first page) when null. Minimum: 1. Used together with limit for standard pagination pattern.

search.description: Search term to filter comments by their content. Performs case-insensitive partial match. Leave empty or null to skip content filtering.
search.x-autobe-specification: Search parameter for filtering comments by content. When provided, performs case-insensitive LIKE query: WHERE content ILIKE '%search%'. Searches discussion_board_comments.content column for partial matches. Null means no content filter applied. Trimming recommended before query execution.

IDiscussionBoardComment.IRequest.description: Request parameters for retrieving a paginated list of comments on an article. Supports searching within comment content and standard pagination controls. All parameters are optional - omit to use default pagination settings.
IDiscussionBoardComment.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: Request DTO for comment list pagination and search. Used as query parameters in PATCH /discussionBoard/articles/{articleId}/comments endpoint. Properties control pagination (limit, page) and content filtering (search). The article context comes from path parameter {articleId}, not request body. Implementation: page and limit compute OFFSET and LIMIT for SQL query; search performs case-insensitive LIKE query on discussion_board_comments.content column when provided. All fields optional with sensible defaults (page=1, limit=20, search=null).

isBanned.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the user is currently banned from the platform. When true, the user cannot log in or access platform features, but their existing content remains visible.
isBanned.x-autobe-specification: Derived from discussion_board_users.is_banned column via primary query. Query: SELECT is_banned FROM discussion_board_users WHERE id = userId (path parameter). Returns boolean indicating current ban status. When true, the user cannot authenticate or access the platform. This column is the authoritative source for ban status in the system.

ban.description: Ban record details when the user is currently banned, or null if the user is not banned. When present, contains the ban reason, administrator who performed the action, and timestamp for administrative transparency.
ban.x-autobe-specification: Computed property populated via secondary query when isBanned is true. Query: SELECT b.id, b.reason, b.created_at FROM discussion_board_bans b WHERE b.discussion_board_user_id = userId ORDER BY b.created_at DESC LIMIT 1. Includes JOIN to discussion_board_users for administrator details via discussion_board_administrator_id. Returns IDiscussionBoardBan.ISummary containing id, reason, created_at, user (banned user), and administrator (who performed the ban). Administrator is nullable if admin account was soft-deleted. Returns null when user is not banned.

IDiscussionBoardBanStatus.description: Response object representing a user's current ban status. Contains a boolean flag indicating whether the user is currently banned from the platform. When the user is banned, includes the complete ban record with reason, the administrator who performed the ban action, and the timestamp. When the user is not banned, the ban field is null. Used by administrators to verify user moderation status before taking further actions.
IDiscussionBoardBanStatus.x-autobe-specification: Computed response type aggregating ban status from two database sources. Primary query: SELECT is_banned FROM discussion_board_users WHERE id = userId. If is_banned = true, secondary query: SELECT b.id, b.reason, b.created_at, u.display_name, u.email, a.display_name, a.email FROM discussion_board_bans b JOIN discussion_board_users u ON b.discussion_board_user_id = u.id LEFT JOIN discussion_board_users a ON b.discussion_board_administrator_id = a.id WHERE b.discussion_board_user_id = userId ORDER BY b.created_at DESC LIMIT 1. Returns: isBanned (boolean from users.is_banned), ban (IDiscussionBoardBan.ISummary or null). Administrator may be null if the admin account was soft-deleted.

id.description: Unique identifier for the file attachment.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_article_files.id. UUID primary key auto-generated on file creation. Used to uniquely identify the file attachment for retrieval and download operations.

original_filename.description: Original filename as uploaded by the user, preserved for display and download.
original_filename.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_article_files.original_filename. Preserves the user's uploaded filename for display and download purposes. Maximum 255 characters. Used as the download filename header.

storage_path.description: Server-side storage path for file retrieval.
storage_path.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_article_files.storage_path. Server-side file location path used internally for file retrieval operations. Not exposed to end users in download URLs.

file_size.description: File size in bytes, used for quota enforcement.
file_size.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_article_files.file_size. Integer value in bytes for quota tracking and validation. Individual files limited to 10MB (10,485,760 bytes). Used for total article quota enforcement (50MB max).

mime_type.description: MIME type of the file, used for download content-type headers and validation.
mime_type.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_article_files.mime_type. MIME type string validated against allowed document formats (PDF, DOC/DOCX, TXT, RTF, XLS/XLSX, CSV, PPT/PPTX, ZIP/RAR/7Z). Used for Content-Type header during file download.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the file was uploaded.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_article_files.created_at. ISO 8601 timestamp automatically set on file creation. Used for chronological ordering of attachments and audit purposes.

IDiscussionBoardArticleFile.description: File attachment metadata for discussion board articles. Contains original filename preserved for display and download, storage location for file retrieval, file size for quota tracking, and MIME type for validation and download headers. Supports document formats including PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and archive files.
IDiscussionBoardArticleFile.x-autobe-specification: Read DTO mapping from discussion_board_article_files table. All scalar columns exposed directly: id (UUID primary key, auto-generated), original_filename (preserved from user upload, max 255 chars for display/download), storage_path (server-side file location for retrieval operations), file_size (integer bytes for quota validation, max 10MB per file), mime_type (validated against allowed document types for content-type headers), created_at (upload timestamp, auto-set). FK column discussion_board_article_id excluded - resolved from path parameter {articleId} in parent operation context. Article relation excluded - prevents circular dependency; parent article accessible via separate endpoint. Files cascade deleted when parent article is removed.

functions.content:
import { IDiscussionBoardArticle } from "@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api/lib/structures/IDiscussionBoardArticle";
import { IDiscussionBoardArticleFile } from "@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api/lib/structures/IDiscussionBoardArticleFile";
import { IDiscussionBoardArticleImage } from "@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api/lib/structures/IDiscussionBoardArticleImage";
import { IEntity } from "@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api/lib/structures/IEntity";
import { DeepPartial } from "@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api/lib/typings/DeepPartial";
import { ArrayUtil, RandomGenerator } from "@nestia/e2e";
import { randint } from "tstl";
import typia, { tags } from "typia";

export function prepare_random_discussion_board_article(
  input?: DeepPartial<IDiscussionBoardArticle.ICreate>,
): IDiscussionBoardArticle.ICreate {
  return {
    title:
      input?.title ??
      RandomGenerator.paragraph({ sentences: 5, wordMin: 3, wordMax: 8 }),
    content:
      input?.content ??
      RandomGenerator.content({
        paragraphs: 3,
        sentenceMin: 5,
        sentenceMax: 15,
      }),
    sectionId: input?.sectionId ?? typia.random<string & tags.Format<"uuid">>(),
    files: input?.files
      ? input.files.map((file) => ({
          original_filename:
            file.original_filename ?? RandomGenerator.name(2) + ".pdf",
          storage_path:
            file.storage_path ?? typia.random<string & tags.Format<"uri">>(),
          file_size:
            file.file_size ??
            typia.random<
              number &
                tags.Type<"int32"> &
                tags.Minimum<1024> &
                tags.Maximum<10485760>
            >(),
          mime_type:
            file.mime_type ??
            RandomGenerator.pick([
              "application/pdf",
              "application/msword",
              "text/plain",
              "application/zip",
            ] as const),
        }))
      : undefined,
    images: input?.images
      ? input.images.map((img) => ({
          original_filename:
            img.original_filename ?? RandomGenerator.name(1) + ".jpg",
          storage_path:
            img.storage_path ?? typia.random<string & tags.Format<"uri">>(),
          file_size:
            img.file_size ??
            typia.random<
              number &
                tags.Type<"int32"> &
                tags.Minimum<1024> &
                tags.Maximum<5242880>
            >(),
          mime_type:
            img.mime_type ??
            RandomGenerator.pick([
              "image/jpeg",
              "image/png",
              "image/gif",
              "image/webp",
            ] as const),
          width:
            img.width ??
            typia.random<
              number &
                tags.Type<"int32"> &
                tags.Minimum<100> &
                tags.Maximum<2000>
            >(),
          height:
            img.height ??
            typia.random<
              number &
                tags.Type<"int32"> &
                tags.Minimum<100> &
                tags.Maximum<2000>
            >(),
        }))
      : undefined,
    tags: input?.tags
      ? input.tags.map(
          (tag) => tag ?? RandomGenerator.alphaNumeric(8).toLowerCase(),
        )
      : ArrayUtil.repeat(
          typia.random<
            number & tags.Type<"uint32"> & tags.Minimum<1> & tags.Maximum<5>
          >(),
          () => RandomGenerator.alphaNumeric(8).toLowerCase(),
        ),
  };
}

scenario.draft: Test successful user registration on the discussion board platform. Verify that a new user can register with valid email, password (meeting security requirements: min 8 chars, uppercase, lowercase, number, special character), and display name. Validate that the response contains: 1) Valid JWT access token (verify it can be decoded with correct claims: sub/userId, email, permission_level), 2) Valid refresh token, 3) Correct expiration timestamps (access token ~15 min, refresh token ~7 days), 4) User profile with correct default values: permission_level='MEMBER', is_banned=false, articleCount=0, commentCount=0, 5) Email matches the registration email, 6) Display name matches request. Also verify that subsequent authenticated API calls work using the returned access token in Authorization header.

dependencies.purpose:
Essential authentication prerequisite:
This join operation (post /discussionBoard/auth/user/join) must be executed before any operations requiring 'user' actor authorization.
It establishes the necessary user account and authentication context for the 'user' actor, enabling subsequent API calls that depend on this specific authorization level.
Without this join operation, the main scenario endpoint and its dependencies will fail due to insufficient authentication credentials.

functions.name: test_api_user_join_success

scenario.draft: Test duplicate email rejection during user registration. First, successfully register a user with email 'test@example.com' and valid credentials. Then attempt to register a second user with the same email but different password and display name. Verify that the second registration fails with a business logic error indicating the email is already registered (not a validation 400 error, but a proper business constraint violation). Confirm that the error response does not leak whether the email exists through consistent error messaging (security best practice). Verify that the original user account remains intact and can still authenticate.

dependencies.purpose:
Essential authentication prerequisite:
This join operation (post /discussionBoard/auth/user/join) must be executed before any operations requiring 'user' actor authorization.
It establishes the necessary user account and authentication context for the 'user' actor, enabling subsequent API calls that depend on this specific authorization level.
Without this join operation, the main scenario endpoint and its dependencies will fail due to insufficient authentication credentials.

functions.name: test_api_user_join_duplicate_email

scenario.draft: Test successful user login with valid credentials. First, create a new user account via join with a valid email, password meeting security requirements, and display name. Then, call the login endpoint with the same email and password credentials along with session context (href, referrer, ip). Validate that the response returns: (1) valid JWT access token (15-minute expiry), (2) valid refresh token (7-day expiry), (3) correct user profile including id, displayName, email, permission_level as MEMBER, (4) computed fields like memberSince, articleCount, commentCount. Also verify the tokens can be used for subsequent authenticated API calls. This tests the primary happy path for user authentication on the discussion board.

dependencies.purpose: Create a user account with valid credentials (email, password, displayName) to enable login testing. Join provides immediate authentication tokens and creates the user record needed for the login operation.

functions.name: test_api_user_login_success

scenario.draft: Test that banned users cannot login to the platform. This is a critical security and moderation workflow. First, create a regular user account via join. Then, authenticate as an administrator (admin join) and ban the newly created user via the ban endpoint with a reason. Finally, attempt to login with the banned user's credentials. Validate that the response returns AUTH_USER_BANNED error with the ban reason displayed, rather than successful authentication. This verifies that the platform properly enforces user bans at the authentication layer, preventing banned users from accessing their accounts while informing them of their ban status.

dependencies.purpose: Create the user account that will be banned. This user will later attempt to login and be rejected due to their banned status.

scenario.draft:
Test that the system prevents demoting the last remaining super administrator.

Preconditions (assumed from test database setup):
- Only one active super administrator exists in the system
- Another user (actor) needs to be a super admin for this test - so actually need 2 super admins where one attempts to demote the other, but there's a constraint

Revised Scenario:
- Setup: Two super administrators exist
- Actor: Super admin A
- Target: Super admin B (the last other super admin)
- Demote Super admin B, leaving only Super admin A
- Then attempt to demote Super admin A (self-demotion - covered in scenario 2)

Alternative approach:
1. Setup with two super administrators (Actor and Target)
2. Actor demotes Target successfully (Target becomes ADMINISTRATOR)
3. Verify Actor is now the only super admin
4. Attempt for a different super admin to demote Actor (but there's no other super admin)

Better Test Flow:
1. Authenticate as a super administrator (Actor)
2. Ensure target is the only OTHER super administrator in the system
3. Successfully demote the target super admin
4. Verify Actor is now the only remaining super admin
5. Attempt to demote the Actor by creating a scenario where Actor tries to demote themselves (already covered)

Final Test Flow:
1. Setup: Two super administrators exist (Actor and Target)
2. Actor demotes Target → Target becomes ADMINISTRATOR
3. Actor is now the sole super admin
4. Any attempt to demote Actor would be self-demotion (scenario 2)

For this specific scenario, test that demotion fails when it would leave zero super admins:
1. Setup state where only one super admin exists
2. This scenario is implicitly tested when:
   - Count of super admins = 1
   - Any demotion would leave 0
   - But that one super admin can't demote themselves anyway

Actually, the business rule 'at least one super admin must remain' prevents:
- When there are 2 super admins, and one tries to demote the other to leave only 1
- This should SUCCEED (leaving 1 is valid)
- The rule prevents demotion that would leave 0 super admins

Correct Test:
1. Setup: One super administrator (Actor), one administrator (Target - not super)
2. Actor cannot demote Target (Target is not super admin) - different error

The 'last super admin' rule applies when:
- There are N super admins
- Demotion would leave N-1 super admins
- If N-1 = 0, reject

Test:
1. Setup: Two super administrators exist
2. Authenticate as one super admin (Actor)
3. Demote the other super admin (Target)
4. Verify success (one super admin remains = Actor)
5. Verify cannot demote Actor (self-demotion protection)
6. System maintains at least one super admin

This validates the rule indirectly - the combination of 'no self-demotion' and 'at least one must remain' ensures system always has super admins.

instruction:
## User Account Business Logic
- Users sign up with email and password (password must be hashed)
- Users log in with email and password (validate credentials, return JWT token)
- Users can change their password (verify old password, hash new password)
- Users can delete their account (cascade delete all articles, comments, and related data)

## User Profile Business Logic
- Each user has a profile with: display name and bio text
- Users can edit their own display name and bio
- Users can view other users' profiles
- A user's profile shows their articles and comments (paginated)

## Section Business Logic
- Sections are created and managed by administrators only (check admin role)
- Each section has unique name and description
- Users can view the list of all sections
- Users can browse articles within a specific section

## Article Business Logic
- Users can create articles in any section (validate section exists)
- Title and content are required
- Handle file and image attachments (store paths/URLs)
- Handle tags (free text, store as array or separate table)
- Users can edit their own articles only (check ownership)
- Users can delete their own articles (cascade delete comments and attachments)
- Administrators can delete any article

## Article List Business Logic
- Paginate article lists (default page size)
- Show title, author info, tags, comment count, created_at
- Sort by created_at: newest first or oldest first
- Do not show full content in list

## Article Search Business Logic
- Search by title or content (case-insensitive partial match)
- Filter by tags (exact match on tag name)
- Paginate search results

## Comment Business Logic
- Users can write comments on any article (validate article exists)
- Comments are single-level (no parent_id for nesting)
- Comments sorted by created_at ascending (oldest first)
- Users can edit their own comments only
- Users can delete their own comments
- Administrators can delete any comment

## Administrator Request Business Logic
- Any user can submit a request to become an administrator with a reason
- Request status: pending, approved, rejected
- Super administrators can view pending requests
- Super administrators can approve or reject requests
- When approved: create administrator record with grade "regular"

## Administrator Management Business Logic
- Two grades: "regular" and "super"
- Super administrators can promote regular to super
- Super administrators can demote other super to regular
- Super administrators cannot demote themselves (validation check)

## Banning Business Logic
- Administrators can ban users (record reason and banned_at timestamp)
- Banned users cannot log in (check ban status during login)
- Banned users' articles and comments remain visible
- Administrators can unban users
- Administrators can view list of banned users with ban reasons

## Authorization Rules
- Regular users: can only edit/delete their own content
- Administrators: can delete any article, any comment, ban/unban users, manage sections
- Super administrators: all admin powers + approve admin requests + promote/demote admins
